body:
We must stop these suppressive bills in the Senate, because the opponents of voting rights in the House keep trying to check these voter suppression bills off their to-do list.
Why? Listen to Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut:
(Image of Richard Blumenthal speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_RB.jpg]
RUSH $35 or more right now to stop these bills, defend our right to vote, and stop opponents of voting rights from destroying our democracy >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060726_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
After the House passed the SAVE America Act ( the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act ), the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections , folks.
Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $35 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060726_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060726_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060726_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060726_3&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060726_3&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060726_3&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060726_3&amount=35]
We know the SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before November, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE America Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060726_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=060726_3&amount=20]
Donate Now [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=060726_3&amount=20]

clean_body: We need leaders who go to the mat for our democracy | | | “I never could have anticipated that I would be facing jail time for doing my job. But here we are.” Those were the words of Fulton County Commissioner Dana Barrett when Republicans tried to get her put in jail for refusing to confirm two election deniers for the Fulton County Board of Elections. She didn’t back down. She’s committed to defending the freedom to vote. Now she’s running for Georgia Secretary of State, our top elections office — and we’ve got her back. = If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: | = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- Take it from Stacey Abrams, who just personally endorsed Dana Barrett: “I am proud to endorse Dana Barrett for Secretary of State because she has the record, the experience, and the backbone to stand up to anyone who seeks to undermine our elections. “On the Fulton County Commission, Dana protected Georgia’s elections from MAGA interference, defending the integrity of elections and making sure every vote counts. Dana is a proven fighter who will never give up on us.” —Stacey Abrams Meanwhile, on the Republican side, one of the remaining candidates is an election denier who called himself “the Black Donald Trump.” The other has pushed for voter suppression legislation in the Georgia General Assembly. And remember: on January 2, 2021, when Trump was working furiously to overturn the election he’d lost, he got on the phone with Georgia’s Secretary of State and told him to “find 11,780 votes" to flip the results. We must make sure that the next person who holds that seat — who could take the next version of that phone call — is someone who’s committed to upholding free and fair elections. Dear Members of Congress,

As of today, I urgently demand you to pass the new bill that would remove Donald Trump from office.

**This simply can’t wait. We have to hold him accountable. Right now.**

| | Friends,
I recently had the opportunity to speak at the Republican Attorneys General Association (RAGA) National Summer Meeting, and it was a privilege to connect with so many leaders, advocates, and supporters about the importance of our race here in Michigan.
I am grateful to RAGA for its continued support, especially Chairman & Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen and the entire RAGA team. Their commitment to electing strong conservative attorneys general across the country is making a real difference.
I also want to extend my sincere thanks to former Michigan Attorney General and former RAGA Chairman Bill Schuette for joining me at the event. AG Schuette has been an outstanding mentor, and I am honored to have both his support and his friendship as we continue this campaign.
[Friends, the nation is watching what happens in Michigan.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rYjxmuqVOpOVeSCSbG-0y5-DD6oVjRA9JwS_OdY_uXfOtF5zV4zWP7lCt5h2c7l1f3wOGR1YYKznnZ2mE623QxvmOe5rrdY7HFUms92INjx2Y92FF-TO_qTVqgDVVbm6rI1lqN94EUH7G63uGQSGYtt0QOM-PyqvA4wK8xQiHGioNBj--K2ZR0wdpaV7IT-hatUlNNipxmWFShtCHB-nVwipO0N6tg9t&c=MDF3dKayR5YBaK81t7v8Pz0HvfT-eAJxjbGqv4daYN5Wqqa_EGdXfQ==&ch=R8-B1Qn8rLtp3OcbC3D5lPX5ywQfsqJsE1nhrCYXjiVJSy5lliVJ1g==)
Our campaign continues to build momentum, and the response we have received from voters across the state has been incredible. Recent polling has shown us in the lead, and our coalition continues to grow every day. Business owners, community leaders, law enforcement supporters, grassroots activists, and hardworking Michigan families are coming together behind our campaign because they know our state deserves strong leadership and a commitment to the rule of law.
[To keep this momentum growing, I need your help today. If you believe in our mission and want to help us build a winning campaign, please consider making a contribution. Every dollar helps us communicate our message, reach more voters, and continue building the organization necessary to win next November.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rYjxmuqVOpOVeSCSbG-0y5-DD6oVjRA9JwS_OdY_uXfOtF5zV4zWP7lCt5h2c7l1f3wOGR1YYKznnZ2mE623QxvmOe5rrdY7HFUms92INjx2Y92FF-TO_qTVqgDVVbm6rI1lqN94EUH7G63uGQSGYtt0QOM-PyqvA4wK8xQiHGioNBj--K2ZR0wdpaV7IT-hatUlNNipxmWFShtCHB-nV34oPUwhJVPP&c=MDF3dKayR5YBaK81t7v8Pz0HvfT-eAJxjbGqv4daYN5Wqqa_EGdXfQ==&ch=R8-B1Qn8rLtp3OcbC3D5lPX5ywQfsqJsE1nhrCYXjiVJSy5lliVJ1g==)
Not everyone is in a position to contribute financially, and that's okay. [One of the most valuable ways you can support our campaign is by volunteering your time.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rYjxmuqVOpOVeSCSbG-0y5-DD6oVjRA9JwS_OdY_uXfOtF5zV4zWP4pmACz1MGp7J1-gDjssmrnab3XmMZ-wX0KNbbjhxr7oEioIg4EqIOevmJmi02HV-P6zzSLH1_FieuLnU7LNPLOXafi_-kf7yefI9w_URiQlJKE6ZNKj5LjbP7WgGUxrEw==&c=MDF3dKayR5YBaK81t7v8Pz0HvfT-eAJxjbGqv4daYN5Wqqa_EGdXfQ==&ch=R8-B1Qn8rLtp3OcbC3D5lPX5ywQfsqJsE1nhrCYXjiVJSy5lliVJ1g==) Whether it's making phone calls, knocking doors, hosting an event, displaying a yard sign, or helping us connect with voters in your community, your involvement can make a real difference. Campaigns are won by people who are willing to step up and get involved, and we would be honored to have you on our team.
This race is about the future of Michigan. It is about restoring confidence in our institutions, protecting our communities, and ensuring that our laws are enforced fairly and consistently.
The stakes could not be higher. While our campaign continues to gain strength, our opponents will have significant resources at their disposal. We must continue expanding our grassroots operation, strengthening our digital outreach, and connecting with voters in every corner of the state. [Your financial support makes that possible.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rYjxmuqVOpOVeSCSbG-0y5-DD6oVjRA9JwS_OdY_uXfOtF5zV4zWP7lCt5h2c7l1f3wOGR1YYKznnZ2mE623QxvmOe5rrdY7HFUms92INjx2Y92FF-TO_qTVqgDVVbm6rI1lqN94EUH7G63uGQSGYtt0QOM-PyqvA4wK8xQiHGioNBj--K2ZR0wdpaV7IT-hatUlNNipxmWFShtCHB-nV1-WbOT3J1_N&c=MDF3dKayR5YBaK81t7v8Pz0HvfT-eAJxjbGqv4daYN5Wqqa_EGdXfQ==&ch=R8-B1Qn8rLtp3OcbC3D5lPX5ywQfsqJsE1nhrCYXjiVJSy5lliVJ1g==)
We are building a broad, statewide coalition capable of winning in November, but we cannot do it without your support. * Repeal of gay marriage and LGBTQ rights
* Suspension of habeas corpus allowing for indefinite imprisonment of political rivals

## Israel Strikes Iran after Missile Exchange
Israel struck military targets in western and central Iran early Monday in retaliation for [Iranian missile barrages](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykULuupDAU-xroQHlAIEWKbehm2y1RSE5mzm5IUHIGNH-_4kr3C25n2ZZl-89jfViMmJ6_7Q6GQl4TXDUCEZSVyns_KuWy1_ymHDARlBPhWgUTqmOqY_PqLcbPOrTeBAABsgXDp5lpLvmo2pfROiip-cYnLp1jXClpnXLKjz7Ms5AtmjuNKTZzxsZx6LWbRrG5IPQGQc-iGRh4pFz6vxkTvSDETz6h9C7vbTQvoqM28lcjlkYs13X1aXP3ilu_mVyib8SCxaZGLBFP6LaYn9_4fXhLUDusxULsbltXqeA_qF1xycpBjaNqi_HHhTFiVVMzsOduMX41oB_ddhrxPwAA__9TNYMl) launched toward northern Israel on Sunday. Blasts were heard in Tehran, Tabriz, and Isfahan. The chain of escalation began Sunday when Israel struck [a Hezbollah command center in Beirut's southern suburbs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLEOmzAURb_GbEbmgQ0MHrqwpWtHZPBz8lpjI_slNH9fJb_Q5S5XOkc6v27rzVGkdP_pDrQc8prwqhGZsaxcnsdZOZej5ifnQImxvAivFRQYqYxU0-odxfc6NN4GRMC-QduNk5q7vtOmeVjjAXw_9LOejNZbFyYM2isd5t3vbjcN2Q9NGTV1Smk9tPM-atj2APOGYZ5ADAo9cS7t70yJHxjiO7-wtHs-mmgfzGcV_Q8Bi4Dluq7W_aVcP6-A5cMWsKjvjAIWqsVhlJUL_cEqI24u5SQ3pPJkScUlWbCeOVWU3wBNsf68KEaqZhSDuh-O4tfN_xXsZeFfAAAA__8liIDp) after Hezbollah fired missiles at northern Israel. Israel notified the Trump administration beforehand, and a U.S. official said Washington supports Israel's right to self-defense. Iran's parliament speaker called U.S. and Israeli bases in the region "legitimate targets." A U.S. defense official told reporters that American forces are "[prepared for defense](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb8GNiLzMLYZPHTJlq4d0cN-Dq8yGNlOovTrK_oLHa-udHXP-brNN-TI-_0TN7I1pHmnV4lUK-W55sd2lJryVtKjpsB7pfxkes0gQHVCdcLMHjm-Z9l6G4iAhpZsr42Y-qEfVbtaN6LXYekdKK_Ie2cMLiDBSae1ctSyPdeEEqYXYhzlZXJ6hMUFmBYKk4FGCvJcU758J97rSiG-05PyxaWtjXat9SjN8NHAtYErHifAWZ0hV3aRGrhyxr17lM4RFgqcqVvpZ0kx4tpxyUixA-ON0FJSPwGS8KNzpAccURgMk1Bttv54cYxclG6kuG_I8e9D_Ze4p4XfAAAA____iINL)" in case Iran follows through. The escalation threatens to unravel the U.S.-brokered ceasefire, which Hezbollah rejected last week. President Trump told reporters he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to tell him to stand down: _"Each of them had their fun. We don't need another one."_
## Trump Walks Out of NBC Interview
President Trump [cut short a _Meet the Press_ interview](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwR0RXmxsFxR_4y5_e6VFzBLvBUwEm1h5-1NS3AtcPdKMvvk6L2dHkfbrf5fQcsjLjkeNyIxl4fJI98q5pJofnAPtjOVJeCygwEhlpBoX7yi-lq7xNiAC6gZtO4xqanXbm2azZkDtBrVq3Qd9WUetvUFtWj0ZNH4wDdl3mzJqbJXq--40rUMPlzXAdMEwjSA6hZ44l9N3pp03DPGVn1hOa05NtBvzvQr9T8AsYOYNN4rxnQmYt5zwDRIwO59op8rFMeVdwNxPrR5VJz9Kebh4qzI_WB4Yb1jkL1bA3BTr7wfFSNUMolPX5Ogz0fCfPnta-AkAAP__46qCWg) with NBC's Kristen Welker after a heated exchange over his claims that elections in California and in 2020 were rigged. Trump called the network, the host, and California election officials "crooked" before removing his microphone and walking away. _"Let's call it quits because I've had enough,"_[he told Welker](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdBOZwRgoXGxDl223RPyMgzfGRvYkXN7-ihT3BW4zzUhH53z_7sN9dN6Fx99xI8M2DoGO7ImZ0sDpte2ZY9pyfHG0LjClt6NjQIkapAbZDsvo_DmoYjGWCKkqyJRNK7uyKmtdrMbSMtVdqVWrlF6WUk-VrrHB0eqqko0qnLloUsu2lLKu1a2bmxqn2WI3ke1aFErS4jim2__oAq9k_RnflG5z3ApvVuY9i-qPwF5gH849Zr5eAvsLLLCXn9MI7F8Zrj6B_acNMqe4ZYjWwkbEwCvBnihn-GmF0TIlsI7SCfQ1r2N4EByOVwjTnOGZXGYKcJB_UoJLDFCiBPI0s4tBYF8ks-yH895l3QglH9vo_Eeff7X52-B3AAAA___ZM5fq). The exchange escalated after Welker pressed him on the proposed $1.776 billion anti-weaponization fund and whether Jan. 6 participants should receive payouts. [Watch the exchange here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFupDAQxvGnMd2i8RgMFC5Ot9purzslSoMMHi9ODF6ZAcTbR5tXSPt90q_4v937uw0xLI9_dibDPvULHWskZso9521-rpzyvKaNkw8LU94DHT0C6gvoC7S9syGefVU444mQVEFGNi10UslaF5ORAyjZUTP6Cq3z2qF14EA57bHzIxTBvDTQ0EqAuq7KbmxqHEaP3UC-a1FUQC5wyuVnCgtP5OOZdsrlmOYimon5uQr1R-BN4O04jvJMG28Dvf7XYnmchLrtQl3pbz4_4vuj-f8lULNQV6nXIhv3PEKMYdWNqOAx2xB_cP5Vkd3gdwAAAP__rZJ1pg). Welker said she and Trump spoke afterward, and he agreed to a follow-up interview at a later date.
## Thousands Protest Kushner Resort in Albania
Thousands of Albanians have [taken to the streets](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OtCAYha8GOwyiohYUX2M3X7ul4edlZAbBwOu43v3GvYXtTnKSk_M8X4_loXzw8flfbSDRpSXCWQIgQl4wH9teMOWtpAOT8xEhfzycC2dcUCYoGxerfLiWrrLSAXBoK5DNMLKpaZteVKsc9SCs6vnYNNZYZ4RunLC6bdnghtGZyst7jQk2Noz1fVdPZui5No5PGtw0ctIxsB5Trl_JR1zBhSt9INcmbVWQK-JeSPuP8Jnw-TzP2uhyU9w94fMdCZ9fKoOl76OsETLVyrzB0nB8H_miGUrKSAumNxRq1VVocnTPCaFgoT5SFbSKXhE-V1na_fQh-CIG0rHnpnz4vYJ_8veR_CcAAP__6JGJCQ) for more than a week to protest a $1.6 billion luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner's investment firm on the country's Adriatic coast. The project would transform Sazan Island, a former secret communist military base and a nearby protected wetland home to [flamingos, monk seals, and sea turtle nesting sites,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ8GOiOzGAOFi7-hu79NiQysDyfGRuvlyL19RF4h7Yw0mu_7eEwP64OPz_92R8MuTRGvHJAZaWI69yNzoj2nk5PzkZFeHq8JJGghtZD9tFof3pMqV-MQAZsSTd31cqibutXlZpoO6lm1Sq-2a9pOg0WpllY7tagOnSy9udekln0tZduqali6FubFwTCjG3oolMTVc6LqM_nIG7rwTi-kakl7GczGfOSi-VfAWMB4XVcV5-WmuPs7SRTWAkY8KR1YwPh15i0iiXB-n_QWhDkRiyPYKA5KjJmzsGG20VtBS7SN6nUNJZn1uHwIPuuuUPK5Wx9-L_CfvL0M_AQAAP__XRyEhQ) into a high-end tourist destination. Protesters say bulldozers moved onto the site with no public consultation. Demonstrators carrying cardboard flamingos and signs reading "Albania is not for sale" have clashed with police, who responded with water cannons. Albania's anti-corruption office has [opened an investigation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHSmzAQBOCngU4eIYOAgiKNuz9tSkZGh7nk0HlOJ4jz9Bn7Ff5-Z2f3-_U1fwUkTI-fYYdJV54TnJlAFWRWKfszK8ueuSivmBTkQDhnZ5031hs7zDEgvea2jtMK4OBaw9T0gx2ba9P5epv8OoTej34ZYfEhxga6GNvo-mUMvnG2xundZr0dGmu7rr2MS9-5-7K68Q7rOLiqtRBRWS6_GZNusNKLD5DLwntN06b6zNX1R-Vulbud53lZuIhuXDK8z7xjlbuFbO6FKPI_kGyEicxKYcf0YCNwMBVFTgakPDUbTCbQPSQMJjwCpqzmT8lbAjEfFUPlb5GXEcgsWrlbLVN8nkiE2fdVax97QPos1G-xHpP7HwAA__-XYJMv) into how the land was acquired. Prime Minister Edi Rama insists the project will go ahead, calling it transformational for one of Europe's poorest economies. Ivanka Trump said she and Kushner discovered the island while sailing with friends: _"We swam to the island. We went on a hike, barefoot all the way up to the top, and we were just captivated."_

My ancestors have lived and died in Maine as far back as the Ancestry records go. And, as some of you know, my first child just turned one-month-old. So I've had a lot of late nights covered in baby vomit to think about, _inter alia_ , my hopes and dreams for her future. I would love for her to have the kind of childhood I had, in the kind of Maine I remember growing up.
Alas, that Maine no longer exists.
But it was not inevitable that the Maine so many of us are nostalgic for would transform into a blighted land of rural poverty and de-industrialization. It was not inevitable that Portland, Lewiston, Bangor, and our other cities would become wastelands of social chaos thanks to socialist-communist policies and crony capitalism masquerading as NGO do-gooderism. None of this was the result of inevitable forces beyond the control of Mainers. It was all the result of hundreds of little choices Mainers collectively made to embrace a political experiment that has, by every conceivable standard, failed.
Mainers chose to experiment with San Francisco-style policies for nearly a decade. The only good thing that emerged from that experiment is that we proved beyond a reasonable doubt that progressive ideas make life worse for everyone but a handful of political elites. Now, we have the opportunity to begin making new choices, better choices. Choices based on the evidence we've painstakingly accumulated through eight years of decline, malaise, and suffering.
On Tuesday, when voters head to the polls for the primary election, the single most important race will be the GOP primary. Because it is in that race that we will get our first indication of whether conservatives can successfully implement a winning electoral strategy, as opposed to a spasm of rage that just feels good but ultimately accomplishes nothing. By Wednesday morning, we'll have a pretty good idea whether Maine Republicans have chosen a winning leader who can alter the fate of this state or a man who can merely lodge a spirited protest.
If it's the latter, I'll probably start teaching my daughter Spanish, because I'll be running the _Robinson Report_ and _The Maine Wire_ from El Salvador -- just one more of the thousands of young Maine families eying the exits because Augusta has become a criminal enterprise and honest working people are the victims.

### My endorsement...
Obviously I'm voting for Troy Jackson. He's a big dummy and he makes me laugh. But for those of you who are pulling a GOP ballot... there are two ways to vote in a Republican primary.
The first is the way most are tempted to vote. We vote for the candidate who says the thing we've wanted someone to say out loud for ten years. We vote for the man who makes the establishment flinch, who goes viral, who fights. We vote, in other words, with the part of us that is exhausted and furious -- and God knows there is plenty in Augusta to make us furious.
The second way of voting is harder. You sit down, you set the anger aside for one afternoon, and you ask a single calculated question: Which of these candidates can actually beat a Democrat on November 3?
That is the only question that matters Tuesday. Not which candidate you'd most enjoy retweeting, hearing on the radio, or the one with the wittiest lines at the debate. Not which one drew the loudest applause at a county committee meeting. Which one wins in the fall -- because the fall is the whole game, and a primary win that leads to a November loss is worse than no win at all.
Let me say that plainly, because this is the entirety of my endorsement: Vote for the man most likely to emerge victorious in November. In my view, the distance -- ideologically -- between the GOP candidates can be measured in millimeters, whereas the distance between most normal Mainers and the potential leftist nominees is measured in miles. But my endorsement boils down to a version of William F. Buckley Jr.'s maxim that conservatives ought to vote for "the rightwardmost viable candidate" -- though I'm erring more on the side of viability.
Put differently, a vote for a Republican who cannot win the general election is, in every practical sense, a vote for Shenna Bellows or Nirav Shah or Troy Jackson. It is a donation to the other side. It's an in-kind contribution to the people who've driven our schools into the ground, our energy bills through the roof, and our young people to freer, fairer states. It's a helping hand to the little lawmakers whose top priority is keeping boys in girls' sports, raising taxes even higher, and funneling money into NGOs that only exacerbate homelessness and drug addiction. And it is worse than a wasted vote in one race, because of what it drags down with it.

## The down-ballot consequences
The governor's race does not happen in a vacuum. The conservative name atop the November ballot sets the weather for every legislative, county, and municipal race beneath it. A nominee who is bleeding independents and moderates, who is defined by billionaire-funded propaganda campaigns before the primary is even settled, who can't raise money and can't stay on a debate stage -- that nominee doesn't just lose his own race. He suppresses Republican turnout and energizes Democratic turnout in the very House and Senate districts where control of the Legislature will be decided by a few hundred votes.
Control of the Legislature is not a consolation prize. In Maine, the Legislature -- not the voters -- elects the constitutional officers. The Secretary of State. The Attorney General. The Treasurer. The State Auditor. If Republicans field a top-of-ticket candidate who tanks the down-ballot races, the Democratic majority survives, and that majority will turn around and hand Aaron Frey two more years as attorney general. Lord knows what he'll get up to in that sound-proofed office of his with another two years weaponizing the Attorney General's Office. The far left majority will install Shenna Bellows as secretary of state again -- two more years of sneaky, deceptive, and untrustworthy administration of elections. More ballots randomly arriving in Amazon Prime packages.
So understand the stakes of an unelectable nominee in full. It is not merely that we lose the Blaine House. It is that we lose the Blaine House and we re-up the very officials who have spent a decade weaponizing their offices against the people who pay for them. You do not get to be angry at Shenna Bellows and then cast a primary vote that guarantees her a $170k-per-year contract extension. Those two things cannot live in the same mind.

## The stakes are existential for Maine
The stakes of this election are not simply protecting our girls, adjusting marginal tax rates, or abolishing the rank policy that steals from households to pay out-of-state solar developers. Those are real, and we've covered them at length at _The Maine Wire_ , and they matter. But they are only part of what's at stake in this election.
The real stakes are existential. They are nothing less than whether Maine has a future as a place where ordinary working people can build a life. Maine stands at a fork in the road. One path leads to a future where the coastal elite, immunized from the harm of their politics by their wealth, enjoy beachfront estates, while the rest of Maine turns into a conservation park speckled with African refugee camps and a few Medicaid agencies. The young leave. The families don't form. The lights stay on for tourists and second-home owners and almost no one else. Sadly, that's the path where our political and cultural inertia is leading. That's the path we're on.
But there is another, brighter and better way. However, choosing to take this happier path requires us to recognize the obvious thing that ten years of progressive experimentation has now proven beyond serious dispute: the progressive program has made life in Maine worse. Not marginally worse. Worse in every single way that social science, economics, and political science can measure. Everything is worse and nothing is better after voters handed progressives _carte blanche_ over the levers of political power. Things are worse on the metrics that decide whether a 28-year-old electrician stays in Lewiston or leaves for New Hampshire -- energy costs, housing costs, the tax burden, the sense that the government in Augusta works for someone other than you, unfettered organized crime, extremists injecting politics into schools while children can't read. We did the experiment. We have the results. The results are bad. Now is the time for us to make political decisions based on evidence and prudence, not emotion and virtue signaling.
That is why conservatives must rank their primary ballot not according to what feels good but according to what is most likely to fundamentally alter the trajectory of the state. The next governor either begins to reverse this undeniable social and cultural decline, or presides over Maine's continued deterioration.

## So what are we actually looking for?
If electability is the question, then we need to be specific and unsentimental about what makes a candidate electable in a state Donald Trump has never carried, where more than 70 percent of registered voters are either independents or registered Democrats. Here are just a few of the items that contribute to general election viability. Apply it to all the candidates and consider the results. Be honest about the answers even when the honest answer stings.
**Is he reasonably financed?** A modern statewide campaign in Maine costs real money -- for television, for digital, for the field operation that actually drags ballots to the box. You do not have to love any of those facts. You do have to look at them clearly, because a candidate who is broke in June is a candidate who gets buried in October.
**Has he built a team?** Not a fan club -- a team. Professionals who can run a modern campaign and who understand that communication today happens on social media, on the radio, and on television all at once, and that you have to be good at all three. A viral social media post is not a field program. Look hard at which of these men has surrounded himself with people who have actually won races in Maine.
**Does he have a compelling, honest story that connects with the average Maine voter?** Not a story that thrills the room at a Republican convention -- a story that lands with the nurse in Saco and the contractor in Caribou who have never been to a convention and never will. And the word honest is doing real work in that sentence. A biography that doesn't survive contact with the press is not an asset; it is a time bomb with a November fuse.
**Is he someone you 'd invite to a barbecue full of your family and friends? **I am not being glib. Maine voters elect people they can stand to have in their living room for four years. Would you trust this man to babysit your kids? Would you want him at the table when your in-laws are over? Likability is not a frivolous metric in a general election -- it is frequently _the_ metric, and it is the one consultants are invariably blind to if their salaries are high enough.
**Is he a team player who understands what November is actually for?** This is the big one, and it's where ranked-choice voting changes everything. November is not about one man securing one room in the Blaine House. It is about assembling the governing coalition -- a conservative Legislature, a conservative slate of constitutional officers, a working majority -- without which not one promised reform ever becomes law. Hell, we'd be lightyears better off just to have normal non-leftists in any of those leadership positions. A candidate who treats the nomination as a personal coronation and a beauty pageant, who won't share a debate stage with his rivals, who won't link arms with the rest of the ticket, is telling you he doesn't understand the job. Watch how he treats the other Republicans. That's how he'll treat the legislators he'll need to make good on any campaign promise.
**Is his personal life in order?** The alleged domestic abuser, serial liar, and habitual adulterer poised to win the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination underscores this point plainly. How a man organizes his own household is the truest available preview of how he will organize any institution placed in his care. A man who cannot govern his own affairs will not govern a $12 billion enterprise with 12,000 employees. This is not about perfection -- none of us qualify on perfection. It is about order, discipline, and the basic competence to run a life before you ask to run a state.
I am not telling you whom to rank first. I am telling you to rank your ballot according to who is most likely to persuade the 351,000 independent voters -- and some of the 326,000 Democratic voters -- that the time has come to end this miserable experiment in left-wing extremism.

### Conservatives must master Ranked Choice Voting
You must rank your ballot. If you don't rank, you're diluting your voting power. [Libby Palanza has written an excellent explainer on how Ranked Choice Voting works.](https://substack.com/redirect/45db3f87-6d9b-42fb-899c-bd95e5c19a5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Yes, RCV is stupid. It's awful policy. But until something changes in Maine, it's how elections will work. So if you don't learn how to rank your ballot, you're disenfranchising yourself.
Rank the candidates who best meet the test above -- first, second, third, and all the way down. Do not bullet-vote one name across the first slot out of loyalty or spite, or rank number one and leave the rest of your ballot blank. A blank second choice is a gift to the other party's coalition. It exhausts your ballot and means you don't get a say in the nominee if your candidate gets bounced. Fill in the whole ballot, top to bottom, in the order of who can actually win.
If conservative voters walk into the booth Tuesday and vote on emotion -- if we reward the candidate who best channels our fury rather than the candidate who can best lead a sea change in the fall -- then January will not bring the inauguration Maine needs. It will not be a referendum that finally punishes Portland-area socialists for doubling and tripling and quadrupling down on their failed and depraved agenda. It will be the opposite of that. It will be an escalation. It will be a further radicalization of the very politics that brought Maine to rock bottom, now with a fresh four-year mandate and a Legislature still firmly in the hands of the people who are profiting from the _status quo._

How a man organizes his own household is the truest available preview of how he will organize any institution placed in his care. A man who cannot govern his own affairs will not govern a $12 billion enterprise with 12,000 employees. This is not about perfection -- none of us qualify on perfection. It is about order, discipline, and the basic competence to run a life before you ask to run a state. I am not telling you whom to rank first. I am telling you to rank your ballot according to who is most likely to persuade the 351,000 independent voters -- and some of the 326,000 Democratic voters -- that the time has come to end this miserable experiment in left-wing extremism. ? Conservatives must master Ranked Choice Voting You must rank your ballot. If you don't rank, you're diluting your voting power. Yes, RCV is stupid. It's awful policy. But until something changes in Maine, it's how elections will work. So if you don't learn how to rank your ballot, you're disenfranchising yourself. Rank the candidates who best meet the test above -- first, second, third, and all the way down. Do not bullet-vote one name across the first slot out of loyalty or spite, or rank number one and leave the rest of your ballot blank. A blank second choice is a gift to the other party's coalition. It exhausts your ballot and means you don't get a say in the nominee if your candidate gets bounced. Fill in the whole ballot, top to bottom, in the order of who can actually win. If conservative voters walk into the booth Tuesday and vote on emotion -- if we reward the candidate who best channels our fury rather than the candidate who can best lead a sea change in the fall -- then January will not bring the inauguration Maine needs. It will not be a referendum that finally punishes Portland-area socialists for doubling and tripling and quadrupling down on their failed and depraved agenda. It will be the opposite of that. It will be an escalation. It will be a further radicalization of the very politics that brought Maine to rock bottom, now with a fresh four-year mandate and a Legislature still firmly in the hands of the people who are profiting from the status quo. ## Defense Opens in Karmelo Anthony Trial
Texas prosecutors rested their case Saturday in [the murder trial](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHPozAMBuBfE7YgJ4QAQ4Zb2HrrjcgQU6IGqBJT2n9_atXpW7_Rsmy9z_vvMlwwxLBd_-JKjp_zPmx05kjMlIYbppXijhsv-_biFDBmPjxtgwZtJVgJ7eAxxNdgCu9G8J0qyKmmhU7Z2qhicTDNFslWNSnUMKq2o6buqhlMN_luNEVw72dgoVUKtGpK35rWVMpAZWtUDQkD5APvqeSFmJ6Y5_jaH5TKaV-L6BbmexbVH6F7ofvzPMtpzG_Fey90_zkRuo_hQfK4e2T6OcqvVH6pcj2SpyQ_ZDkjY5SZcRzDdpV4ZA6bXIknjLOcU8jTLjnhdJMrEQvdF8n5-xliDNk2wsB1xRA_cfl3JT-c_h8AAP__SUCVUA) of Karmelo Anthony, 19, accused of fatally stabbing 17-year-old Austin Metcalf at a Frisco high school track meet last year. After four days of testimony--including autopsy details, teen eyewitnesses, and a medical examiner--the defense began presenting its case Saturday, arguing Anthony acted in [self-defense](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O6zAMBODTyJ0DUZFlpVDxGnd57ZYGHdExEVkKZObv9osEucH2BGe--TmOR-TE-fwfVwrynMuY6bElEqE6XrCulApmWUp-SWVMm9wi5dFo41rtWu3HiJxeo21imHQ8QEMBeq8P4DoLzRIcxB6sPxHABD7OXUdIBHjoqZt8Rw2H9zPttAfQBvpd9NbbPVi9dx1CT8pqiiyl7mQhoSduc3qVO9XdqaxNCovIdVP7f8oMygzv-hmFS87l8b5QZjhVXkmZ4etpv6B2vdVItf3A2kvmmdpNcJo4n5UZmhri9cEp8eZ6ZfV5RU6fTPnbUvdgfgMAAP__js1_rQ). Anthony faces up to life in prison if convicted. The defense [opened by calling three witnesses](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHSqyAQBeCn0Q4HEBELitvY5ba3dDayRm4QMrDG5O3_MZM3-Lstds6c7_y7TBfwwcfbX9jQ0mtJU8SjBCTCPN0hbxgSRFpTfFP2EArtDuMkudSMa8bN5MCH96RqZ6_cDaJGK3rDB6E7JerVguzVwI1wgzQgNMy9uEI39LLjrTbK1N6eYVxzIwSXom-cUUa1QvFWdyB6rBRH5ynlhlYkfEFZwjs9MTdz2upgV6JHqdo_lRwrOR7H0SzppU7G-VDJ8TwrOX417MthHw8L_olsfzggLAz2Qj6yDWmGsLAl-zInRhnmO9sQif3fIzJdZ-sehw_BF91Xit828OHThn634dPKnwAAAP__n5KIDw)--Anthony's track coach, a teammate, and a Memorial student--all of whom reinforced that athletes routinely mingled under other teams' tents, while the coach also highlighted Anthony's 2024 Team Captain Award.
## Mayor Advocates for Selling City Hall
Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson unveiled a proposal to [sell City Hall](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUD2TpCAQ_TWYMQXIoBMQXGK2l15o9UC7UtuCBX26_vsr9y9c-r7qvffnY_6ARCl__oYNPX8vZc54NkJmrPMX1A2pQOa15ItrAmr8N2KejTJOKifVOEdIdM22i_6t4kt36PUwqpd2T6u71b-fOC69BjW6JVineh2eqNUrLuE9xDh0yd9hyqlRa2X08IijHW2vrerdE_SAwiqMiUt98IqM39AWusqB9RHK1pFfmfcm-l_CTMJM53k-wrvdK25emOnHIsx0Q8JMKZScgoxABE2GxJdcgUhucJUqsaYgy5pbyXIrB8qGRHKvZcfKl9zguBVfTTaG2uROkIuM5cxczizM1FUf9zMRpeYGYdXnBol-ivL_3Xt48y8AAP__Jg6TlA), arguing that the move would help save the city money for downtown redevelopment and perhaps anchor a bid to keep the Dallas Stars from moving to Plano. The Mavericks entered into an option agreement for a [$50.76 million land deal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO5iAQBODT4IxfDcavgGATZ7PphlYDzRhN-yFg7Plvv_JeYdMq6VOp_nwsH5g47Z-_cSNbf-Kx7HQXplopL1-YN-ID97oe-7vmhFzqd6B90aB7Cb2EcQmY-L2YJlgHYVINWTWMMKm-M6pZrfIwKVDaG41t7AKZqfXRjc4pRIxTk-yDQQ-jUqDV8AqjGU2rDLR9h2ogYYBCqkd-1ZUq_WCJ_D4uyi9_bA3btdaziPaX0LPQ833frzsiPqXQM-aaPJPQczmPXIvQ8-5Q6HnDi3LyX08SkBmL3PAq8kJmessr0S03ZJbnd_YrFpJnTv6B9DhINTpUnQ_SwxCk6ZyTru-dDBDR-NgZmKYm23DeiTmVfhAGPjdM_G9z_b-nL6v_BgAA___8U5Ix) at the former Valley View site off the LBJ Freeway and Dallas North Tollway in Dallas, while the Stars have said they intend to build a new arena in Plano, along with restaurants, residential units, and retail shops in the Willow Bend Mall area. The mayor said that the teams' decisions to move out of downtown are not yet final: "_The Valley View site that the Mavericks are looking at, it's in Dallas, that's a good thing. ... But as far as the Stars are concerned ... from my understanding, it is a letter of intent. It is not a final dea_ l." Mayor Johnson argued that selling the beloved building--a target of preservation advocates--could fund a revitalized downtown core, which may convince the sports franchises and others to stay downtown.
## Spurs Face Must-Win Game 3 Tonight
The San Antonio Spurs head to Madison Square Garden tonight [trailing 2-0](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0b2OpDAQBOCnMZlHduPhJyC4hGwvvRA1uJmxxrSR2yzL259mXmHjUpX0qf59TV8YYuDHX9xoKD9rmphOiVQK5emFeaOYkMsz8VVywCjl8MQTGGi0abTpJo8hXpOr_DAb39uKBtt2prfN3dnqOXgPrSPfOLP4ztZLUxP1ALXFfqH5DlUY3mOmMZ21Bmx7853rXG2dqZs72paUM-RDSflWnlToB2WNV_qmfFvSVsXhWcouqv6jYFQwnud5I9n5HSoYeUYFo5SULwXjpGAMXsHour4Da0DB-KHwjHoNjFH0AzfSoPeIV1pX0UynvlJ-6ReH5SVakDVySRySlv3IosO2p1yQy6ckOpJIYtFLOnLRJ20z8oUb6jkfLImrPPj9DDEGaVrlzGPDED-Y8rsLvgf4HwAA__97L51r) in the best-of-seven series, after Victor Wembanyama's late miscommunication with Stephon Castle handed the Knicks a one-point Game 2 win in San Antonio. The Knicks are [picked to win the series by oddsmakers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAQRp9GM61uZJAJCDYxm003tFrBgVoEC3p-fPtbM69w86--c-r8u803CjGk-1_aneH3lufkXjU6Zlfm_1R2FzMl9jmdXALFyg_r0ixAqA5UB3q2FOI5y9aaBewVW2dw1HBFdZHYejMg6GUZNhhX2iyMV8R1ABqEXoRSC7TBfM5AgUYEgWNvtdRyQAmDuhCOrpHgbOBcevaO3ZvqFs_8dKVf895G45mP2gx_GjE1YqpHLlz7k3zOn0EjJioc1uhqI6avd1qoWz3tR8ip-nB02drasX8k60qHF0AAKbD3vMe2GHu8QoyhqrGRcN8pxC-Yf5fracRPAAAA__8yFn5Z). # [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1100?t=1&akid=660%2E3892029%2EPe4t9K)

Over the weekend, we joined a huge parade in The Villages in Florida. It’s one of the largest retirement communities in the world — and also a place that hasn’t voted blue for president since 1996. I am humbled by the amount of people who showed up.
You see, when I was first deciding whether to run for Senate, I knew that we had to build a big tent in order to win. And we have _a lot_ of ground to cover.
Florida is one of the most populous states in the country, and we need to share our message with as many folks as possible. That means reaching out to people online, at their doorstep, or even via golf cart.
The good news is, we have a plan to do that: In the coming days, we’re hoping to hire a few more organizers on the ground and increase our digital advertising. This could truly make the difference in an election as close as ours — but we can’t do any of it without your help.

Hello all, I hope your summer is off to a great start. It snuck up quickly on us, didn't it?
I was back on [CNBC](https://substack.com/redirect/7b7fe609-8481-421b-bdc1-f5791e28cc9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this week to make the case that we should tax AI - and eventually robots - and not humans. They invited me back because I think they're worried about the impact of AI.
First, the big question - is AI going to displace human workers? Of course it is. You're going to spend a trillion dollars on AI infrastructure and data centers... and then it won't affect the labor market? That doesn't make any sense. You need to have corporations paying hundreds of billions of dollars a year for AI in order to justify the trillion-dollar IPO valuations for OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic. That money's got to come from somewhere, and workers' wages are the obvious source.
Let's say the AI companies' revenues continue to grow. Right now, they still won't pay meaningful taxes because they are still losing billions of dollars and not generating taxable income. So you're in the worst of both worlds - a diminishing need for human labor and no new tax revenue to show for it.
We have made people expensive to employ in myriad ways. For example, let's say I hire a new whippersnapper at Noble Mobile. My costs will include 10% or so in FICA, state unemployment insurance and other payroll taxes. I'll pay another 10% or so for that person's healthcare. Then, the worker will pay 15-25% in income taxes depending. That's almost half of the amount I might budget for this person that he or she won't see in their take-home pay, all of which discourages both me from creating the position and hiring and the worker from accepting and showing up on Monday.
Or, I could use Claude or some AI tool to do the work. I pay Anthropic for some tokens and... that's it. No payroll tax. No healthcare. No income tax.
We have set up a system that dramatically advantages AI when it doesn't need the help to compete.
So what do we do? We need to try to balance the scales by taxing AI and then lift the taxes on people. Tax AI, not humans.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eed71c2b-66c3-4667-a214-4121a68323cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This isn't just me talking.
Dario Amodei of Anthropic says, "You should tax AI via a token tax."
Sam Altman says, "Create a national wealth fund via AI revenue."
Vinod Khosla says, "Don't tax the bottom 80% of workers."
John Arnold says, "We should tax compute to make workers more competitive."
A lot of smart people are figuring out that we have set ourselves up for a calamitous picture because we punish employers for hiring human beings relative to machines.
Addressing this imbalance is going to be one of the biggest challenges of our time. Are our leaders and institutions up for the challenge?
Of course not. Trump is doing whatever he's doing and the Democrats are jockeying for position and lying in wait for the '28 primary.
Multiple trillion-dollar AI IPOs are on tap - we are likely to mint the world's first trillionaire - and things are changing quickly. What to make of these impending IPOs? The valuations don't make sense at the topline - and the S&P 500 just balked at changing its rules to accommodate SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic. That said, I have never seen so many banks bending over backwards to encourage investment in an IPO. I have the feeling that being first out of the gate will be a lot better than being third given the amounts of demand needed to soak up these shares.
It's unprecedented.
If we're going to bet the economy and everyone's retirement savings on AI, the least we could do is tax it.

Regaining the court conventionally is no longer feasible. The only path forward for Democrats is taking unprecedented action to break the conservative stranglehold over the Supreme Court.
This is why Defend Our Courts exists. Our plan is the only way forward for Democrats -- and it works on two tracks simultaneously:
Track one: Win state Supreme Court races to build the firewall that protects voting rights, blocks gerrymandered maps, and holds the line at the level where elections are actually decided. We beat their machine in Pennsylvania. We beat it again in Wisconsin. We have more races to win in November and beyond.
Track two: Build the political will to unpack and reform the United States Supreme Court -- which requires winning House majorities, Senate majorities, and the presidency, because we need all three to expand the court. Neither track is easy. Neither is cheap. Both are necessary. And we have already proven the model works. What we cannot do is run this program without you.

GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE

Friend,

I want to start with two simple words.

Thank you.

Thank you for caring about children you may never meet.

Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold.

Because that is exactly what is happening.

Every day.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b2AojEWDBzvamucOe_0yWNynHPPJqY1ipV2Nmb_idYoDD072vXx8AVjV_j9P7teExuWU5ei_WSlbhmR6gQmhmXbfhaU2WU3R42Jg

God's children are not for sale.

And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth.

When you make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation today, we'll send you a FREE white "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b33YOVynZ75iSeFzG-paLZE3K7RrJOVBOyF9_oeLk4fBSWOXjqzdO-LrBFWgI_FgQ7kjpOB8a5k0r-ver2hrFpEkdCbZkhxe7U1g

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b45cYylK5csWeyysms23Ii56yNMjp0IDaKBeQgDRXRPamiZbcAlS4XTRoKvoDm4maGqji7E3RQ_yEfmuI5tufg2_cZQsOXfRK4vA

This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store.

You can't buy it online.

It was created exclusively for supporters of the Sound of Freedom Foundation.

People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say:

"No more."

Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters.

A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity.

And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see.

Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.

A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children.

Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission.

Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b5j0Ac5SdrdJmORgV_8_DuBsZ8lf_xxD_rfSjBSoRqkz0F9CXk9KVIzhcjd9Qi28jiXBXOBGKlrykzzbG1LgROsjwmivelOeqUPQ
Protect God's Children Today

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me.

My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart.

Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed.

I couldn't forget it.

I couldn't stay silent.

I kept asking myself one question:

"What if it were my child?"

That question changed my life.

What started as a film project became a mission and a calling.

That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom.

Not for fame.
Not for awards.
But because I believed people needed to see the truth.

For years, many people said the film would never succeed.

Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up.

But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.

And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough.

That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation.

Our mission is simple:

To stop the sale of God's children.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b6DXsNd_3NvTlcoKKeDirS93CLQtzckJfLsU65zVRC4ykWcslApTNFAvmWe4HqMr2syJlTWPQPrxGVX6hLe4EmYo2NoWrauX4onQ
Protect God's Children Today

Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear.

And every day, we work to fight back.

Jesus said,

"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14)

Every child is precious in God's eyes.

Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.

And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b7jA2e9rdLoejKeM0e12-hcnIAr8rj0XnUf4-BsVRNVfivF511kDzUx6yi3ZfhFMCBuvrSB7LE0rNkF6BK3iTIuNbS4Mc5q1Mybg

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDF9AAwAAAAAARJbE8b8xxUo4Eu80kZBRjCHG5ugwdLfsvY4ha2sTar_y2-LVa_gMsPUuX7yINdOBjmjQkC07fb3LC_yMv1wPy8XEvg7_94gr_f243O4Cg
Protect God's Children Today

When you make your first gift today, you help:

- Prevent exploitation by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children.

- Support intervention efforts by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation.

- Educate parents and communities about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

- Raise awareness so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

- Advocate for stronger protections for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

This is how change happens.

One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.

Today, that person can be you.

## 100 Days In, Trump Says He's "Very Close" on Iran — and Ready to Strike if He Isn't
Marking 100 days since the first strikes on Iran, President Trump sat down with NBC's "Meet the Press" Sunday and laid out where things stand: a deal is within reach, but he's not signing anything that lets Tehran keep the bomb. He said the U.S. is "very close" to an agreement while pushing for tougher nuclear guarantees.What He Said
* ▸ If a deal comes together, Trump said American forces would help **retrieve and destroy** Iran's highly enriched uranium — on-site or hauled off entirely.
* ▸ If Tehran refuses, he warned the U.S. would **further degrade Iran's military** until American forces could collect the material safely on their own.
* ▸ Trump claimed Iran's navy, air force, and anti-aircraft systems have been effectively **wiped out** , calling the campaign a "military exercise," not an endless war.

Why It MattersThis is the America First doctrine in action — leverage first, concessions never. Trump kept the door open to peace while making clear the military option stays on the table. He also tied it straight to your wallet, predicting that once a deal is done, **gas prices are "going to drop like a rock."** Read the full story at [Axios](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_Hys5gLMiMt2YvhfA3lnJ7Z_9qngfjwBXpos9Zm7zkrwQTvfkSZ37BxZ2HubN6fIZ8ByHZ7lq8xk-4x2Quqr_qYJBIKvoqJfygjyojbYctA28RBG97xgVJ7ErKJ0Gvr98tUvsbAYB7Q12FkN70M7cD2MdVPDkDsPsi0A6LL5vm-oGfBrX75JfacOKIegPlBGFYjDBgtPxjOYHhekg_PwxVl61fL7QIS9IVD_oB-rNMcZSyisUriDoDg-3jHlVdtDXej0uRz8-UNsOjFsaK6lMyxUeMiIaFV5160aO5OdUamO9cs5c_Q14GXClGDXDUnchQ/4rb/i0yf7RtfTHKpXKnLbKBRSQ/h1/h001.aQY4jjKTywHjsslPamQXUVhxzuZGMIptMMwtYbxEfhA).

## Jobs Boom Puts Trump and the Fed on a Collision Course
The American worker just delivered a blowout. May payrolls surged by **172,000** — topping every forecast — in a sign the economy is humming despite the Middle East energy shock. But there's a catch: Wall Street now expects the Federal Reserve to read that strength as a reason to **raise** interest rates.The Fight
* ▸ Trump isn't having it. A rate hike is "the wrong thing to do," he said — the Fed should be **cutting** , not squeezing families and businesses.
* ▸ New Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** , a Trump pick, chairs his first policy meeting **June 16-17** , walking into a divided committee.
* ▸ Gas above **$4 a gallon** has pushed inflation near **3.8%** , complicating the case for cuts.

The PerspectiveHere's the absurdity Trump is calling out: good news for working Americans gets punished by markets that assume the Fed will hike. A strong jobs report should be cause for celebration, not a trigger for higher borrowing costs. If the Iran deal lands and energy prices fall, the inflation excuse evaporates — and the path to lower rates clears.Read the full story at [Bloomberg](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.helAEltPsJerhr4Tfhlii2RKv-3o7D-_UJKth_Mm9M62gIk8okWu82kkfS9sQth9XiSrVi6QTx_CKVqsQtor9OaElcnDnS2XVevx1ZodaliFgEH4PEFm5a-2r7MBzgfaxKML4L_vVimJKhFnzp5XrfFQUkWzvjUS-RgGl-bwJWe38L4zyeh4uSaIH82ROAj65OFT2TJyzJ5hI3qrVUNAJ0Ow-YflzzZ1STKjoKdEi_paE69Yb7loPFt1zWBT-WFj8PiQKHAEgVPMWv5rHTD-743suMAjfR8aGeeSZ8oy5RajfdMeMsGmEoS6k2mb0un87c1f_lvzrmNpvuYEn9PRjQ/4rb/i0yf7RtfTHKpXKnLbKBRSQ/h4/h001._3L3pkIGehQp0OFaHKx5z0gtR0PM_hJAuH8C4Qq4NZg).

★ The Border
## $70 Billion Border Bill Heads to the House — With One Flashpoint Lingering
Fresh off its pre-dawn Senate passage Friday, Trump's **$70 billion** package to fund ICE and the Border Patrol now moves to the House for final approval. It would lock in enforcement funding through the end of his term and shield the agencies from future shutdown fights.The Sticking Point
* ▸ The administration told the courts in writing that the controversial **$1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund is dead** — the concession that finally freed the bill.
* ▸ But on Sunday, Trump reopened the debate, saying some people prosecuted over **Jan. 6** "should be compensated" on a case-by-case basis.
* ▸ That puts House Republicans in a familiar spot: deliver the border win without reigniting a fight the Senate just put to bed.

Why It MattersBorder security was the promise that defined the campaign, and this bill is the hard funding behind it. The faster the House moves, the sooner the agencies get certainty — and the sooner the GOP can point to a concrete deliverable heading into the midterms.Read the full story at [CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NvJs1xljQ5GNMxZ64aW7B_g8qKJTJZMcDbgEOLj8N2RE-X_PMGnyrAW8GpR1ArVj86uGDGnuWffRAvXNd9YAcboKJcMXGtzwRgwsPlCGZLgQZUC6ZT0rNTiEQiwj7wcK-VQKJZ-HYkoo8C-hj9BMy1cq2joo7pdQIL2oeXu-KfuMBXsnNyetc3tdTzbW3X3C8f-TyO6vXOS4mbejlz0fLigogz_mgNjU4Qjuo7zoHfql6xOoF_2G4VoQU74pBdysrs3SeqqMm9Lrufh47n2HOkDkELyaUtvU_D9-Jay94TG1j9jaaqApcge4Jn_gYGlGQ/4rb/i0yf7RtfTHKpXKnLbKBRSQ/h5/h001.pBcKujMjVXq_K8BHnSA9CpkQXIz7y0dMKHHgBfIrXcI).
* * *
★ The 2026 Map
## Another Dynasty Test: A Bush Runs as an Outsider in Maine
Voters in Maine head to the polls Tuesday, and one name on the GOP ballot carries a lot of history — Jonathan Bush, nephew of one president and cousin of another, is betting the family name can still win in a party Trump remade. His own ad opens by getting ahead of it: "Not another Bush. I get it."The Stakes
* ▸ Bush's top rival is **Bobby Charles** , a former State Department official running as the field's loudest conservative — and its most polarizing.
* ▸ Maine's **ranked-choice voting** could favor a broadly acceptable second choice, a possible edge for Bush.
* ▸ The race is one of several 2026 contests testing whether **political dynasties** still sell with a populist electorate.

The PerspectiveFrom the Iowa farmer who toppled a sitting congressman to a Bush insisting he's not "another Bush," the 2026 map keeps sending the same signal: voters are done being told who their nominee should be. The brand on the yard sign matters less than whether the candidate sounds like the people they want to represent.Read the full story at [CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NvJs1xljQ5GNMxZ64aW7B_YfOFnZM1tLOIn3_0lZM71rcDJMcZZAp0Q3BcPnFcLGNODzZvxafjJpKQ-CW_aNnxEDVzMMvtcZsjPj3LhpRSczhwhX5N34OvZVxroEramTkhXxlkhYzNXtkx1G-tfaJJrOi2KOc6einF-hbt3skZPZR95ELdcFumxdePC2Ybo3QrHl6En5Mox8pAaML3P11k8L74Hrk4ifygev1DHuP1_ten0Yn1kVNeL2iUU1qsV6eUXiy1X4c3r4xM9AK_W6Gj1NJ80ApHhDZTwbao4KBPw/4rb/i0yf7RtfTHKpXKnLbKBRSQ/h6/h001.-7F29B2bMZbJujxIPs2JOhTIz9JN25K5R19BzMM3wKE).⚡ The Bottom LineOne hundred days into the Iran campaign, Trump is holding the line abroad while the American worker delivers a jobs boom at home — even as the Fed eyes the wrong move. The border bill is one House vote from the finish line, and primary voters keep rewarding outsiders over insiders. **Strength overseas, results in the economy, and a base that wants fighters — not figureheads.** "The truth isn't conservative or liberal. Hemp Meadows (Scott Arvin) is a lifelong musician.
Hemp grew up in a Southern Baptist family where he started out singing gospel music and hymns. "Church provides you a great opportunity to sing," he reminds.
He was enamored with the drums and started playing. He played in the youth symphony and the high school band and studied percussion at the university level. Along the way, the Beatles happened, and he, along with the rest of the world, discovered Rock and Roll. "That changed the trajectory of my life," he recalls.
He wasn't into country music (like Tammy Wynette and George Jones), Opera, or even Frank Sinatra. He was all about The Who, the Rolling Stones and the Beatles.
In his youth, Hemp played drums in numerous local rock bands until they broke up. About that time Crosby, Stills, and Nash came along and their sound was "so enchanting" that he wanted to learn to play guitar as well. He was also compelled by the counter-culture revolution in the late 60s and early 70s.

| | Peter, I understand that organizers don’t have unlimited resources. I understand that sometimes, we have to make tough calls. I understand that big dreams take time to achieve. But I will _never_ understand how anyone could look me in the eyes and tell me that my home state – and everyone living there – isn’t “worth” fighting for. Still, people always ask why we’re so invested in organizing across Florida. They claim that Florida is too red, too far gone, too deep under the thumb of the far-right fascists like Ron DeSantis, and that we can’t “afford” to fight back. **If I’d listened to that kind of defeatism in 2022, I wouldn’t be writing to you today as the first Gen Z member of Congress. And I’m damn sure not listening to it in 2026.** [**_It takes real work to win tough fights. But it’s work we _know_ how to do, and I believe we can do it. **This state is in play, and you won’t catch me on the sidelines when everything from our education to our democracy to our planet’s survival is at stake.

clean_body: | ~ | | Peter, I understand that organizers don’t have unlimited resources. I understand that sometimes, we have to make tough calls. I understand that big dreams take time to achieve. But I will never understand how anyone could look me in the eyes and tell me that my home state – and everyone living there – isn’t “worth” fighting for. Still, people always ask why we’re so invested in organizing across Florida. They claim that Florida is too red, too far gone, too deep under the thumb of the far-right fascists like Ron DeSantis, and that we can’t “afford” to fight back. If I’d listened to that kind of defeatism in 2022, I wouldn’t be writing to you today as the first Gen Z member of Congress. And I’m damn sure not listening to it in 2026. ~ ~ | | ~ Thanks to people like you, chipping in spare change and sometimes digging even deeper, we’ve gained ground in Florida. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132919778/626126702/-153530995?refcode=EM_C_260605Pride_N_SB_90DO_4_NG_N_Logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NjY5YjUzYy00MDYzLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nlnQHV91aFkPSBhW7ToZ9DHtNiDrHq6oXP6pv-dJepk=) Peter, happy Pride Month! 🏳️🌈

In a month of Pride, it’s so important that we not only celebrate the LGBTQI+ community, but we also keep working for progress.

The LGBTQI+ community continues to face discriminatory bills and attacks every single day, both on the state level in Ohio and from the Trump administration, which has made hatred and discrimination a central part of its platform. But let’s never forget how this movement started – at Stonewall – as the very first Pride was a protest for basic human rights. Now, it’s critical that we continue the fight for equality.

**As a member of the Congressional Equality Caucus, I will continue to stand ten toes down in support of LGBTQI+ Ohioans. Together, let's fight against violence and discrimination and work towards a future where justice and equality are the norm for all.**

Onward and Happy Pride,

Shontel Brown | Shontel Brown is proud to be elected as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District. She has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. As she enters her second full term in Congress, she will use that experience to continue the fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and to preserve and protect our democracy for generations to come. Will you join her and be the change we need?

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132921781/626132577/-1080350292?sourceid=1058994&refcode=WUEFER14_20260608_FourGovs_ALL_v1s3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YTc1MzQ0Mi00MjYzLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YMrA0_IgzLLLM2zd7HdkSCfcQryGOHyPi68heG9Qilg=) Peter, this cycle we launched our State Power Plan to help EMILYs List women build the campaigns they need to take back power in state legislatures, governors' mansions, and key offices across the country.

And right now, four of our endorsed candidates for governor are making it clear exactly what's at stake:

**1. Gina Hinojosa** — running to unseat Gov. Greg Abbott in Texas: "Texas Republicans can't pass rigged maps next year if they have a governor who will veto them."

**2. Jocelyn Benson **— running to defeat John James in Michigan: "The power of the people will always be greater than the people in power."

**3. Katie Hobbs**— running to hold her seat in Arizona: "My opponent already tried to overturn the 2020 election in Arizona. We can't give him another chance."

**4. Amy Acton** — running to defeat Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio: "Ohio doesn't need more politicians focused on special interests."

These Democratic women are running to stop Republican extremism, defend our rights, protect our democracy, and deliver for working families. Their wins would be a massive defeat for MAGA Republicans in some of the most consequential races in the country.

But they're up against billionaire Republican mega-donors, outside spending, and nonstop attacks designed to drown out their voices and silence the communities they're fighting for.

**[Peter, we can't let candidates like Gina, Jocelyn, Katie, and Amy fight these attacks alone. Blaise Pascal was right when he said there is a God-shaped vacuum inside every human heart. The question is who -- or what -- we will worship. And increasingly, many young women are being told to look not to God, but to crystals, spells, manifestation, moon rituals, and the worship of self.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9rYXRoeWJhcm5ldHRlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.zMV22Z2spoymsWq9-ZcilV6Zots_2kW5vdWhb1l0XUs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=201058394)
Every one of us will spend our lives organizing ourselves around something:
Some acknowledge God and spend their lives pursuing Him.
Others acknowledge wealth.
Some acknowledge power.
Some acknowledge politics.
Some acknowledge pleasure.
Some acknowledge themselves.
But everyone bows to something.
The Bible tells us that God has made Himself known to all men. Not just through Scripture. Not just through nature. But deep within us. We know there is something greater than ourselves. We know right and wrong exist. We know justice exists. We know beauty exists. We know love exists. We know evil exists. And every human being must decide what to do with that knowledge.
The Apostle Paul says something remarkable in Romans. He doesn't say mankind lacks knowledge of God. He says mankind suppresses the truth. That's different. The issue isn't ignorance. The issue is rebellion. The issue is what we do with the knowledge we've already been given.
And here's where I think we find ourselves as a culture. We have not become less religious. We've become religious about different things. We've replaced the knowledge of God with the worship of self. The highest virtue today is self-expression. The highest authority today is personal desire. The highest commandment today is "be true to yourself." But what if yourself is wrong? What if your desires are disordered? What if truth exists outside of you?
Christianity begins with the opposite premise. It says I am not God. I am accountable to God. Truth doesn't originate with me. Morality doesn't originate with me. Meaning doesn't originate with me. I discover those things in relationship with the One who created me.
Every belief system produces fruit. If God is God, certain fruits follow:
Humility.
Service.
Sacrifice.
Love.
Truth.
Responsibility.
Protection of the vulnerable.
The recognition that every human life possesses dignity because every human life bears the image of God.
But if the self becomes god, different fruits emerge. Everything becomes centered on personal autonomy:
My truth.
My identity.
My desires.
My body.
My choice.
My fulfillment.
My expression.
And eventually society becomes a competition between millions of little gods, each demanding recognition from everyone else.
That's why I don't think the great crisis of our age is political. It's theological.
We have forgotten who God is. And when a civilization forgets God, it doesn't stop believing. It simply starts believing in itself. And history has shown us repeatedly that mankind makes a terrible god.
**People do not stop worshipping God ... they just redirect their worship. **

| Peter,

NY-17 is one of the most competitive congressional districts in the country — and it's our best shot at flipping the House.

Here are three things you need to know two weeks before our primary:
1. **Mike Lawler was one of only three Republicans to win a Congressional seat that Kamala Harris carried in 2024.** This race is _winnable,_ but only if we fight for every vote. The fate of NY-17 and Congress will be decided by the voters who step up, vote, and help us close razor-thin margins.

2. **Every major election forecaster calls NY-17 a toss-up.** We cannot afford to sit this one out.

This race _will be _decided by a few hundred votes. Grassroots donations don't just fund campaigns — they fund the last-minute door-knocks, phone banks, and organizing that will actually move that margin.

Peter, it’s Deb Haaland.
I’m a daughter of Pueblo women, a New Mexican, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **Now, I’m the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
**[Will you split a donation of $5 between Heartland Patriots and my campaign to help us reach our first $50,000 fundraising goal of the general election, keep our momentum going, and win this race in November so I can deliver for working families across New Mexico?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104796?refcode=em20260608-10530&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=2&akid=10530%2E614464%2EyuLHSz)**
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104796?refcode=em20260608-10530&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10530%2E614464%2EyuLHSz)**
I come from generations of Pueblo women who taught me resilience, service, and how to keep going no matter what. My mother served in the U.S. Navy, raised four kids as a military wife, and spent decades in Indian education. My parents didn’t have much, but they believed deeply in giving back and showing up for others. _Those are the lessons that shaped my entire life._
It’s what carried me through working in a bakery after high school, starting a small business, raising my child while relying on food stamps and WIC, and eventually stepping into public service to fight for working families.
**Now I’m running for Governor because I believe every New Mexican deserves a fair shot — no matter where they come from or how much they have.**
But Peter, we know what’s coming. Billionaires and national Republicans are already preparing to spend whatever it takes to flip this seat. And in New Mexico, the governor’s office has a long history of switching parties every eight years — which means this race will be decided by what we build right now, together.
**[So please, will you split a donation of $5 — or anything you can — between Heartland Patriots and my campaign today to keep this momentum going and make sure we’re ready for the fight ahead?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104796?refcode=em20260608-10530&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=4&akid=10530%2E614464%2EyuLHSz)**

Peter, we want to talk about something Iowa should be incredibly proud of:**our leadership in renewable energy.**

_Iowa is a renewable energy powerhouse._ We are the second-largest producer of wind energy in the nation, and nearly 60% of our electricity comes from wind power. Aside from curbing greenhouse gases, wind energy supports thousands of jobs across Iowa and has become a major driver of economic growth. And the future is just as promising. These emails are the best way for our campaign to stay in touch with supporters like you. If you'd prefer to unsubscribe, [click here](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7010?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.08_MS-NOW-RR_B1_F1_S1_C1_tier-1-2_N-T0&t=1&akid=6301%2E196590%2EDW29Pd).

I know that you’ve got a lot going on this week, and chipping into my campaign for Governor isn’t at the top of your to-do list. [**_But give me just one minute to fill you in on why your $5 would mean EVERYTHING ahead of my critical fundraising deadline at midnight!_**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7311?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.08_MS-NOW-RR_B1_F1_S1_C1_tier-1-2_N-T0&t=5&akid=6301%2E196590%2EDW29Pd) | | [ CHIP IN NOW → ](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7311?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.08_MS-NOW-RR_B1_F1_S1_C1_tier-1-2_N-T0&t=6&akid=6301%2E196590%2EDW29Pd)

Trump flew to the Badger State for one reason: to put his finger on the scales for his handpicked candidate for Wisconsin Governor, Tom Tiffany.

_We can’t let Wisconsin fall into MAGA's hands. But if we don’t hit every single fundraising goal, we won’t be able to match Tom Tiffany’s MAGA millions!_

[**_Listen, I don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so falling short right now would be a SERIOUS problem for this campaign. Our team is knocking on doors in every corner of Wisconsin, from Milwaukee to Eau Claire – in small towns and big cities. We're making phone calls and talking to voters who feel forgotten by politicians who only show up at election time. We're raising as much money as we can, dollar by dollar, to compete against the millions in Dark Money pouring into this race. GALA
The Mississippi Center for Public Policy's annual gala, A Celebration of Mississippi's Success, will take place on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at the Country Club of Jackson. Hello,
I’ll get straight to it: **I’m about to ask if you can make a donation to help me defeat Lauren Boebert before our final federally-mandated FEC fundraising deadline before the General Election.**
But first, can I explain why this final FEC deadline is so important?
After Wednesday, federal law requires our campaign against Lauren Boebert to create a report of how much we’ve raised. That report then becomes public.
Reporters and pundits will dig into our report to judge the size and strength of our campaign. But it’s not just reporters.
Lauren Boebert and her Super PACs are going to scour our report to see if Boebert is still in danger. The national Democratic and Republican party are going to see if we have enough grassroots support that they need to prioritize this race.
And this is the last chance for grassroots donors like you to show that you are 100% behind me to help me defeat Lauren Boebert this November.
We’re about to be under a microscope like never before, so we need a show of financial strength unlike any we’ve ever had.
That’s why we’ve set one of our biggest goals ever: **Raising another $250,000 from grassroots donors before this final FEC deadline to show reporters, Boebert’s Super PACs, and the entire Republican and Democratic establishment that we’re still all-in to defeat Lauren Boebert in 2026.**
