Hi Peter,
Thank you for signing up to stay in touch with our campaign! I’m Brad Smith, and I’m running for Congress in Wisconsin’s 6th District because I believe everyone in this district should be represented by someone with deep local roots, who actually has their back. Glenn Grothman no longer engages us, his constituents of the 6th District, and frequently votes against our interests while providing canned form letters in response.
I’ve lived my whole life throughout this district, from being born in unincorporated Larsen, to graduating from Neenah, to now raising my two young boys with my wife Jen in Mequon. I’ve served in the Wisconsin National Guard overseas during the Global War on Terror and have built my career helping businesses grow through digital transformation.
**I’m in this race because the Wisconsin that gave families like mine a fair shot feels like it’s slipping away for too many people, while we see billionaires getting richer than ever.**

### My campaign is focused on three things:

**1️⃣ Good jobs and fair wages for all**
An economy should reward work, not just enrich the people at the top.
**2️⃣ High-quality healthcare access as a right**
No family should go broke because someone got sick.
**3️⃣ Education and training for every path**
College, tech school, apprenticeships, trades, retraining. Every Wisconsinite deserves a real shot.
If you’d like to learn more, here are a few good places to start:
* **Watch my short intro video below 👇**

* **See where I stand on the issues**
[Watch Videos](https://us.list-manage.com/MdONBaI2RhO?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11) or [Read Positions](https://us.list-manage.com/RmxXRaPBTjj?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11) Summary

* **Meet the people backing our campaign**[ View Endorsements](https://us.list-manage.com/pakfvcWcbKU?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11)

* **Follow our campaign on social media** to get the latest scoop[](https://us.list-manage.com/NK39kFiQxgB?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11) [](https://us.list-manage.com/31YsSmAn1jN?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11) [](https://us.list-manage.com/DvVKF6KpA9k?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11) [](https://us.list-manage.com/iUbrW0ylspj?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11)

If you’re interested in getting involved with the campaign, there are a few big ways to help right now:
* **Volunteer with us**
[ Sign Up](https://us.list-manage.com/o0WPkF_Ihee?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11)

* **Chip in to support the campaign**
[ Donate](https://us.list-manage.com/z4MWIjtOOqJ?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11)

* **Put up a yard sign to show your support**[Request a Sign](https://us.list-manage.com/jTfyaTTAD8k?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8&i=de7631ef11)

And one more thing. I’d genuinely like to hear from you.
Hit reply and tell me the issue you care about most in this race. I may not be able to answer every message personally right away, but hearing directly from people across the district is a big part of why I’m doing this.
Thanks for being here. I’m glad you joined us!
Best,Brad Smith
Candidate for Congress, WI-06
P.S. A number of current and former elected leaders who’ve already backed this campaign include former Chair of the Democratic Party of Wisconsin Martha Laning, Representative Maureen McCarville, Senator Melissa Ratcliff, Menasha Mayor Austin Hammond and more. We’re building real momentum, and I’m grateful to have you with us! 🙏

name: Matt Ortega
subject: Thank you
body:
One last email on Tuesday's results, our impact, and the choice going forward. | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVdaU3GDudfHJ-LpMUWeRi9iuVBaY-E6iK8WBYDhBhwkgz6xblv2zBch8_eD9ilKXSQeszP4nb6RXEG7eEtNX9zkPkfX8lqrNYhG85Xs8k5auGcOv7M1iURVYvz80heLaIl0OlgwRDi66pwcFkLe8sU4mLDc5dP93wgsYZalXmryiLYHkOppSGN0QAGHu3yHeEyrp6BvvV0wCo_Yoatmjhw8/4rb/eIEmVNQjRgm9ZK35WakttA/h0/h001.lXOeCScYh2lFclyRancXZ67EKkfZg14ASHWus48zS4o) | Friend, At the outset of this campaign, our goal was to secure a spot on the general election ballot in November. And while the counting continues at this hour, the returns are clear. East Bay voters made their voices heard and in a democracy, the will of the people must be respected even if sometimes the answer is no. To every 14th District voter who placed their trust in this campaign, I am deeply humbled and grateful. The right to vote, purchased at great cost by those who fought, and bled, and died for it, is in the fullest sense, democracy itself. That right, under the greatest threat in generations, is both the people’s shield and their sword. This campaign launched six months ago because the status quo is irreparably broken. This broken status quo is an existential threat to our children’s future—the direct result of politicians too compromised to act boldly. Tuesday’s results did not change the stakes. They confirmed them. **The choice is clear. There is only one candidate with the values, the tenacity, and the breadth of vision to shape the future my sons and your children stand to inherit—and that is Sen. Aisha Wahab.** On the issues confronting the people of the 14th District, Sen. Wahab is the only candidate with the head, the heart, and the stomach for the fights that lie ahead. I urge voters to send her to Congress on June 16 and keep her there on November 3. With our rights threatened and our nation mired in an illegal war, the people of the 14th District can trust Sen. Wahab to fight and protect our communities— _all_ communities. The same cannot be said for her opponent this fall. Hand-picked by the same Washington establishment that continues to fail us, Melissa Hernandez is unprepared for the national stage. And that’s why wealthy interests flooded the district with over $1.5 million to boost her. With her history of selling us out, they know what they’re getting. She will deliver for them—not for you. She was never meant to. The decision to enter this race was about taking on wealthy interests and protecting vulnerable communities. And though we fell short Tuesday, our campaign’s impact is proven by who will also _not_ be on the ballot come November. To my wife Sophia, who bore a greater burden than anyone in this campaign, thank you—for your love, your support, and your commitment. To my sons, Lucca and Nico, I love you boys and your mom dearly. I did everything I could to ensure your future is brighter tomorrow than it is today. This fight does not end with Tuesday’s results. The stakes are clear. The work continues. The moment is now. And in the richest nation on earth, the future we were promised is still worth fighting for. —Matt
---

subject: Pride was born from courage
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260608-2345-foote&t=1001&akid=2345%2E342411%2Ej4sUn3 ]Squad Victory Fund

Happy Pride Month,
Peter! 🏳️🌈🏳️⚧️

Across the world, people are celebrating LGBTQ+ visibility, resilience,
and unapologetic joy.

While the current administration pushes dangerous rhetoric about the
LGBTQ+ community, targets transgender Americans, and works to strip away
access to gender-affirming care — we're showing up anyway. Loudly and
proudly.

Pride was born from protest,
Peter. When people fought back
against the police raids of queer spaces in the 60s and 70s, transgender
leaders like Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera sparked a movement that
transformed our country. The very first Pride marches honored their
courage — and that same spirit continues to fuel the fight for equality
today.

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida have always stood with the LGBTQ+
community. They'll keep showing up, speaking out, and fighting for every
person's right to live openly, safely, and proudly as themselves.

This Pride Month, we uplift and celebrate queer joy, honor the
trailblazers who came before us, and recommit to the fight for dignity and
freedom for all.

In solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Donald Trump and the right are actively trying to erase queer and trans
people from society and target anyone who stands with them.

This Pride Month, we have the opportunity to elect an LGBTQIA+ champion to
represent New York’s 7th district in Congress: Claire Valdez.

Far-right news outlet Breitbart is accusing Claire of supporting a federal
trans bill of rights and publicly-funded gender-affirming care. And, for
once, they’re right!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260608-cv.BlVHI5&refcode=em20260608-37880&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=37880%2E1203867%2Exo4hfM ]A post on X from Breitbart News: 'DSA House candidate Claire Valdez,
endorsed by both Mamdani AND Bernie Sanders, continues campaigning on a
'trans bill of rights at the federal level' and publicly-funded
'gender-affirming care'. 'My role in Congress is to use a bully pulpit to
make sure that we're talking...'' It was reposted by Claire Valdez with
the caption: 'Once again: correct.'

Claire knows it’s not enough to simply defend queer and trans people — we
must proactively fight for everything LGBTQIA+ people deserve.

That means protecting queer and trans people at work and school, ensuring
they can update their government IDs, and giving them the guaranteed right
to gender-affirming care.

If we send her to Congress, this Justice Democrat will do that by fighting
for the Trans Bill of Rights, the Equality Act, and the Transgender
Healthcare Access Act, as well as making sure things like Medicare for All
and affordable housing for all are truly for all, with proper funding and
rights included in legislation.

We only have 15 days left to get out the vote for Claire in one of the
most progressive districts in the country. Let’s make sure this seat stays

body:
Shelley shares deep, personal thoughts about her husband's loss. Campaign trail update.

| | | | |
---
| | **A New Reason to Go Forward **
**Stronger Than Ever**
---
**Greetings, Alaskans: **
**On May 23, I lost my husband and biggest supporter, Roger "Rock" Hughes. I want to thank my family, friends, supporters, people all across Alaska, and my campaign team for the outpouring of love, kindness, and prayers. God’s presence has been very evident since his passing, and I’m grateful for each of you. I want you to know that Rock – or as many knew him, Roger – cared deep for our nation and our state and believed strongly in the principles and values that are the focus this election yeaar.**
**When a man, a combat medic, who’s had soldier dies in his arms, returns home to be literally spit on as he walks through the airport after landing on US soil, you listen to his strong convictions – especially when after all he saw and experienced, his love for his country never faltered. You pay attention to his words. You respect his views. That’s what I did as a young wife. I listened and learned; I began to pay attention, and out of that my own convictions grew. And out of that I became involved.**
**When the flame in my spirit first sparked to step up and serve Alaska, early on before I filed, at times I felt inadequate, ill-equipped. But it was Rock who put his hands on my shoulders and looked me in the eye and got me back on track when he said, “You were made for this. God has given you the strengths, the gifts. Alaska needs you.”**
**He has been my number one fan through thick and thin. When going through photos and mementos with my children, I found a funny valentine he’d made by hand. Along with the love and romance in his note, he signed it “your most loyal constituent.”**
**I want you to know that Rock was absolutely thrilled Blake Gettys joined my ticket. He recognized the leadership and character in Blake like I did. He knew a retired general, a smart, competent, honest leader made our ticket the strongest in the field. Rock summed it up when he said, “Shelley, you struck gold.”**
**In what would turn out to be Rock’s final week, he was apologizing that he didn’t have the strength to put up my signs and be my number one sign-guy as he’d been over the years. I reassured him all was going according to plan and our team had it under control. Rock will smile from heaven as our signs sweep the state in a strong wave.**
**There’s nothing more that he’d want right now than for me to finish this race well and win and help this state, to ensure the next generation is not left with a mess, to ensure that Blake and I can bring pragmatic solutions to fruition that will truly build a strong Alaska.**
**I drew close to family the last two weeks, those here in Alaska and those who flew in from out of town; I was not out campaigning and outlining my action plan -- but know this, I learned from my husband to stay true to my convictions. What I say, I do. My solid track record is proof, both in the private sector and in my more than 12 years in the legislature.**
**Blake and I are not about one-liners and manipulating voters. We are about truth and integrity and getting the job done. Politicians too often disappoint us. They sound so good on the campaign trail but change once in office. You don’t have to worry about that with the Hughes/Gettys ticket. We keep our word. Rock would expect nothing less. **
**As I look toward the future, I know that the man who was the love of my life for forty-eight years and the quiet strength behind all my endeavors will never be far, and forever in my heart. My family and I will live out his legacy every day. We will honor his memory through our lives, through the resolute continuation of the Hughes-Gettys gubernatorial campaign, and a steadfast focus on upholding the principles of this great nation he loved so dearly. **
**Thank you for your incredible, ongoing support. I will continue to fight for Alaska on your behalf. With my return to the campaign trail this weekend in Homer and Kenai, and Blake's leading the force during my two week hiatus, know that we continue to be "in it to win it".**

**Hughes referred to Blake as "Mr. Elections" publicly a few weeks ago but has since decided we should refer to him as "General Elections" since he is after all, (Ret.) General Gettys! Blake knows Alaskans deserve confidence in our elections. That means staying ahead of modern security threats, not ignoring them.**
**Over the last 14 years, various state agencies have experienced multiple data breaches involving sensitive personal information. At the same time, Alaska’s current automatic PFD voter registration process has raised concerns about how applicant data is handled before eligibility is fully vetted.****That combination creates vulnerabilities we cannot afford to ignore.**
**Our position is simple: election integrity and voter access should go hand in hand.**
**That’s why the Hughes/Gettys ticket supports implementing multi-factor authentication for mail-in ballots — a straightforward security measure designed to help ensure ballots are being requested and submitted by the actual voter.**
**This shouldn’t be a partisan issue. **
**Protecting voter confidence should matter to everyone, regardless of political affiliation.**

**"Some places simply change your address. Alaska changes who you are.**
**Like so many others, I came here to work, serve, and build a life, and somewhere along the way, Alaska became home.**
**This state teaches you resilience, sacrifice, responsibility, and what it truly means to serve something bigger than yourself.**
**This is where I served our nation as a Brigadier General. This is where I learned what responsibility really looks like. And this is the state I’m fighting for alongside Shelley Hughes.**
**I believe in Shelley’s vision and action plan for Alaska because it’s centered on something simple: putting Alaskans first, strengthening our communities, protecting our future, and restoring leadership people can trust.**
**Alaska changed my life for the better. Now it’s time to fight for Alaska’s future together."**
_**-Blake Gettys**_

clean_body: Shelley shares deep, personal thoughts about her husband's loss. Campaign trail update. | | | | | | | A New Reason to Go Forward Stronger Than Ever Greetings, Alaskans: On May 23, I lost my husband and biggest supporter, Roger "Rock" Hughes. I want to thank my family, friends, supporters, people all across Alaska, and my campaign team for the outpouring of love, kindness, and prayers. God’s presence has been very evident since his passing, and I’m grateful for each of you. I want you to know that Rock – or as many knew him, Roger – cared deep for our nation and our state and believed strongly in the principles and values that are the focus this election yeaar. When a man, a combat medic, who’s had soldier dies in his arms, returns home to be literally spit on as he walks through the airport after landing on US soil, you listen to his strong convictions – especially when after all he saw and experienced, his love for his country never faltered. You pay attention to his words. You respect his views. That’s what I did as a young wife. I listened and learned; I began to pay attention, and out of that my own convictions grew. And out of that I became involved. When the flame in my spirit first sparked to step up and serve Alaska, early on before I filed, at times I felt inadequate, ill-equipped. But it was Rock who put his hands on my shoulders and looked me in the eye and got me back on track when he said, “You were made for this. God has given you the strengths, the gifts. Alaska needs you.” He has been my number one fan through thick and thin. When going through photos and mementos with my children, I found a funny valentine he’d made by hand. Along with the love and romance in his note, he signed it “your most loyal constituent.” I want you to know that Rock was absolutely thrilled Blake Gettys joined my ticket. He recognized the leadership and character in Blake like I did. He knew a retired general, a smart, competent, honest leader made our ticket the strongest in the field. Rock summed it up when he said, “Shelley, you struck gold.” In what would turn out to be Rock’s final week, he was apologizing that he didn’t have the strength to put up my signs and be my number one sign-guy as he’d been over the years. I reassured him all was going according to plan and our team had it under control. Rock will smile from heaven as our signs sweep the state in a strong wave. There’s nothing more that he’d want right now than for me to finish this race well and win and help this state, to ensure the next generation is not left with a mess, to ensure that Blake and I can bring pragmatic solutions to fruition that will truly build a strong Alaska. I drew close to family the last two weeks, those here in Alaska and those who flew in from out of town; I was not out campaigning and outlining my action plan -- but know this, I learned from my husband to stay true to my convictions. What I say, I do. My solid track record is proof, both in the private sector and in my more than 12 years in the legislature. Blake and I are not about one-liners and manipulating voters. We are about truth and integrity and getting the job done. Politicians too often disappoint us. They sound so good on the campaign trail but change once in office. You don’t have to worry about that with the Hughes/Gettys ticket. We keep our word. Rock would expect nothing less. As I look toward the future, I know that the man who was the love of my life for forty-eight years and the quiet strength behind all my endeavors will never be far, and forever in my heart. My family and I will live out his legacy every day. We will honor his memory through our lives, through the resolute continuation of the Hughes-Gettys gubernatorial campaign, and a steadfast focus on upholding the principles of this great nation he loved so dearly. Thank you for your incredible, ongoing support. I will continue to fight for Alaska on your behalf. With my return to the campaign trail this weekend in Homer and Kenai, and Blake's leading the force during my two week hiatus, know that we continue to be "in it to win it". Shelley HughesRepublican Candidate for Governor of the Great State of Alaska p.s. The August Primary is just 10 weeks away. I need your support to get us to the top for clear victory. Our campaign manager and deputy campaign manager are volunteers so your dollars don't go to salaries like in other gubernatorial campaigns. They go directly to getting our message out. Team, Across the country, millions of Americans are celebrating Pride Month. Here in Tennessee, Bill Lee and the Republican Supermajority used it to pass a resolution declaring only one kind of family worthy of recognition. Their "Nuclear Family Month" resolution defines a family as "one husband, one wife, and any biological, adopted, or fostered children." We know not every Tennessee family fits that box. If you're a single mom working two jobs, a grandparent raising your grandkids, a same-sex couple who built a life together, a blended family, a foster family — **the people running this state just told you that you don't count.** This resolution carries no force of law. But it carries a message: some Tennessee families matter more than others. Here's what they _**aren’t**_ talking about: housing costs that have pushed working families out of the neighborhoods they grew up in. Grocery bills that keep going up. Healthcare that's out of reach for too many. Real problems, real pain, felt by Tennessee families every single day. clean_body: Across the country, millions of Americans are celebrating Pride Month. | = Team, Across the country, millions of Americans are celebrating Pride Month. Here in Tennessee, Bill Lee and the Republican Supermajority used it to pass a resolution declaring only one kind of family worthy of recognition. Their "Nuclear Family Month" resolution defines a family as "one husband, one wife, and any biological, adopted, or fostered children." We know not every Tennessee family fits that box. If you're a single mom working two jobs, a grandparent raising your grandkids, a same-sex couple who built a life together, a blended family, a foster family — the people running this state just told you that you don't count. This resolution carries no force of law. But it carries a message: some Tennessee families matter more than others. Here's what they aren’t talking about: housing costs that have pushed working families out of the neighborhoods they grew up in. Grocery bills that keep going up. Healthcare that's out of reach for too many. Real problems, real pain, felt by Tennessee families every single day. We are running Democrats across the state who will be a voice for EVERY Tennessean — every family structure, every zip code — and protect our fundamental rights. But we can't do it without you. = = | = This month and every month, we stand with EVERY Tennessee family. Thank you for standing with us. # [How Big Oil Wrecked Your Summer](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=201056529&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAxMDU2NTI5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODA5NDY2NDcsImV4cCI6MTc4MzUzODY0NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.SgIImfqSyTTYijNsnWXrn_CZzNElRatSqS8UZplIkWA)
### Americans are facing a dangerous summer of climate disasters--just as Big Oil predicted.
| | [Aaron Regunberg](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---
| Jun 8
---
| [](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=201056529&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAxMDU2NTI5LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc4MDk0NjY0NywiZXhwIjoxNzgzNTM4NjQ3LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItNDk4MTE3MCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.CMzV1pKwRwBoGX1jsmmwfSp3R-cdr9bDZvJ4jNDVsPk&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/aaronregunberg/p/how-big-oil-wrecked-your-summer?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

I love the summer. Growing up, it meant family vacations, beach days, block parties--really, what's not to like? But for millions of Americans, the meaning of summer has been [shifting](https://substack.com/redirect/dd4416d0-7cd6-41f4-bd36-fa3cab269152?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In many parts of the country, excitement for the upcoming season has turned into anxiety over the weather events--the extreme heat, hurricanes, drought, and wildfires--that have increasingly defined our summers in recent years.
These weather extremes are not natural. They are climate disasters. And as a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/95b82056-1259-4b59-a714-42d9a6d8487c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published last week by my organization, Public Citizen, outlines, they are exactly the kind of catastrophes that Big Oil companies predicted their fossil fuel products would cause--at the same time that they were orchestrating fraudulent campaigns of climate denial to block solutions that would have alleviated these harms.
**To put it bluntly, Big Oil is ruining summer.**
Naturally, the most obvious threat is the heat. The last three summers have been the [three hottest](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd51ff1-adfb-4105-ae69-1239c58b37de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ever recorded. Since 1985, [80 percent of U.S. cities](https://substack.com/redirect/1ea31c2c-25ca-4859-8885-0e60db817441?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have experienced an increase in the number of days with a heat index of 90 degrees or higher. This trend has already extended into 2026, with record-smashing heat this spring across the western half of the country, including an average national temperature in March that was an [astounding](https://substack.com/redirect/159b8e3d-c994-40ea-8e4b-06507af88804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 9.35 degrees Fahrenheit hotter than the twentieth-century norm.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..AyD7FOkesquJf2jiECR0jfMOu6xR7YxkhqJN0dve7Xs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=201056529)
This escalation in extreme heat isn't a coincidence. A climate attribution [study](https://substack.com/redirect/b30764dd-16d9-44c4-a6c6-690f059a1915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the March 2026 heat wave found that it would have been "virtually impossible" without climate change. Nationally, scientists have found that the climate crisis [lengthened](https://substack.com/redirect/ec9eea32-e8db-4ef1-9ddb-2e51510ace1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the average heat wave season in the U.S. from 23 days to 70 days over the last 60 years. Another scientific study [concluded](https://substack.com/redirect/6f1e34e9-f436-4f31-a746-45954dcd41a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that last summer, the average American experienced at least one additional week's worth of risky heat days due to climate change, while 32 U.S. cities (home to over 21 million people) experienced 30 or more additional risky heat days.
Scientists are increasingly able to determine the degree to which the emissions of particular oil and gas companies have contributed to particular heat waves. For example, a [study](https://substack.com/redirect/d231e67f-17d2-424f-9316-83c97be6974b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published last fall in the prestigious journal _Nature_ analyzed a number of major heat waves, including the extreme heat that hit the American Southwest in July 2023. The researchers found emissions from each of the biggest fossil fuel companies--ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, Shell, and BP--made that lethal heat wave at least 10,000 times more likely to occur. They concluded that these events would have been virtually impossible without those emissions.
And it's not just that these companies contributed to the oppressive heat that is now defining summer for so many of us--it's that they knew full well what they were doing. For decades, Big Oil companies internally forecast exactly how their fossil fuel products would drive increasing heat, and how we would experience these changes. In 1996, for example, Exxon scientist DJ Devlin gave a [presentation](https://substack.com/redirect/67c385f5-ae5c-43e3-b59c-4811bdd9f3d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Global Climate Coalition, a group of fossil fuel companies that colluded to spread climate denial, reviewing the science connecting climate change with "suffering and death due to thermal extremes." He discussed how the "elderly, sick, and very young" would be particularly vulnerable. And he explained the idea of threshold temperatures, referring to the point at which temperatures cross a critical limit "beyond which mortality rises significantly."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5a24350-6b86-4729-b3c9-3a8257a308b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Presentation by DJ Devlin to Global Climate Coalition, pages 6-9.
While the "thermal extremes" of recent summers have been bad, they occurred during a La Niña, the cooling phase of the Pacific Ocean's heat cycle. But this summer is going to be different. Scientists expect that in the coming months the Pacific Ocean will begin its warming cycle, or El Niño. And this El Niño is [predicted](https://substack.com/redirect/ed6f8560-3ca3-4514-8beb-719cd573ad4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be particularly catastrophic--again, largely due to climate change.
Some [studies](https://substack.com/redirect/cad6fb65-7157-4b5c-9435-c0c632ff7708?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have found that global warming may be leading to stronger El Niño events. More importantly, climate change means that this El Niño will build on a higher [temperature baseline](https://substack.com/redirect/8c48a461-68b4-4acc-88fe-44b7dd5d4abc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which will have the effect of supercharging its impacts. That constitutes a dangerous cycle. As Defense Department meteorologist Eric Webb [put it](https://substack.com/redirect/01cef151-17e4-4e9d-a5cb-71871925ee59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "Due to the increasing concentration of greenhouse gases, the climate system cannot effectively exhaust the heat released in a major El Niño event before the next El Niño comes along and pushes the baseline upward again."
And it's not just heat that will be supercharged this summer. Climate change is also causing a severe intensification of droughts and wildfires across our country, turning summer in many areas into a season of water rationing, air quality alerts, or worse.
The U.S. already experienced its most intense spring drought ever this year, with the first three months of 2026 [being](https://substack.com/redirect/21d08d2d-9486-49b3-a1a3-815262e0658d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the driest on record. Over 60 percent of the country is currently experiencing at least moderate drought. And in many regions, the situation is far more severe.
Ninety-nine percent of the [Southeast](https://substack.com/redirect/293a636d-c14f-4896-bb6c-7f97e6a3b4d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is in drought, with over 60 percent in severe to exceptional drought. This has [spurred](https://substack.com/redirect/10cd199b-ea28-449a-af07-60596d009666?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) record-breaking wildfires across the region--Georgia has already had [eight times](https://substack.com/redirect/0bed2bd0-e0e1-405b-b843-e44cd4a18dc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as many burned acres so far this year compared to the pace of the last five years. The Great Plains region is facing similar challenges. Nearly 90 percent of [Nebraska](https://substack.com/redirect/293a636d-c14f-4896-bb6c-7f97e6a3b4d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is in drought, and the region has already experienced record-breaking spring wildfires that burned over a [million acres](https://substack.com/redirect/04e5b10c-9846-401a-bc5b-c629d7ded2ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of land across Nebraska, Kansas, and Oklahoma. And in the West, extended drought is reaching a tipping point, following the lowest snowpack levels in a century. Utah recently announced a [state of emergency](https://substack.com/redirect/3dd78b9f-0cd2-4406-ac9f-7b86eabc6243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over its water crisis, with the entire state in severe drought and 22 of 29 counties experiencing extreme drought. Colorado, which also relies on snowpack, may [soon](https://substack.com/redirect/d2feeddd-b725-411c-86ee-a660abcbe8a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) follow.
These droughts, and their subsequent impacts on wildfires, are directly related to climate change. Climate scientist Kaitlyn Trudeau [described](https://substack.com/redirect/10cd199b-ea28-449a-af07-60596d009666?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the relationship this way: "Climate change is making the atmosphere thirstier. As it gets hotter, the amount of moisture that is pulled out of the landscape or sucked out of plants and soils also increases." A 2023 [study](https://substack.com/redirect/e8e05fb5-9ca6-4b9c-9b4a-f6dad782caf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the journal _Environmental Research Letters_ found that almost 40 percent of the area burned by wildfires in the western United States over the last several decades can be attributed to the emissions of the world's largest fossil fuel companies. Speaking of the connection between climate change and increasing dryness that is contributing to wildfire growth, the author of the study [said](https://substack.com/redirect/25881fa5-ee7d-43a2-bdd1-fc1b999220e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "I've never had such a strong correlation in my data before."
Big Oil companies understood their role in enabling these climate effects decades ago. In 1981, Exxon scientist Henry Shaw wrote an [internal memorandum](https://substack.com/redirect/2c7fd6c7-e019-4386-9b59-5099feb6ce90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Exxon's president of research and engineering explaining that it was "Exxon's position" that a doubling in atmospheric carbon dioxide from the burning of fossil fuels would result in "major shifts in rainfall." In 1982, the American Petroleum Institute commissioned a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/3070a6d0-11a9-4c36-9386-af85131a3229?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) warning that climate change would have "serious consequences for man's comfort and survival since patterns of aridity and rainfall can change." And in 1998, Shell confidentially [predicted](https://substack.com/redirect/d9175b91-e8a1-4e53-a30c-43ee857376b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that if fossil fuels were not brought under control there would be "more droughts" that would "dramatically change" agricultural patterns and "disrupt eco-systems." Shell even predicted that because of these changes, "conflicts would abound" and "civilization could prove a fragile thing."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0de27d4b-9746-4cfd-b6e5-23004276b938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/147630a1-1661-4faa-b928-302e72234f69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From Shell confidential group planning document, page 36.
Then there are summer storms. Hurricane season began on June 1. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has [predicted](https://substack.com/redirect/d718ef15-b9df-4195-8f6f-4c1bea817184?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a worse than average hurricane season in the Pacific this year (combined with a below-normal season in the Atlantic, where El Niño generally suppresses the number of storms), [forecasting](https://substack.com/redirect/756dca5b-1095-4c30-8358-2c485e93bfd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between three and six hurricanes, including one to three major storms.
Although hurricanes are not new phenomena, climate change is increasing their severity in several ways. Higher sea surface temperatures make hurricanes more likely to intensify--in fact, over the past 40 years, [three times as many](https://substack.com/redirect/137e56af-6310-42b0-9672-9b012dca491d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) storms within a few hundred miles of coasts have intensified rapidly due to warming of the oceans. Storms are also staying [stronger](https://substack.com/redirect/6eb194e7-5eba-4ccf-afe4-d0ad0a4ada7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) farther inland than they did in the past, with warmer sea surface temperatures leading to a "slower decay" of storms by increasing the amount of moisture they can carry. They are [generating](https://substack.com/redirect/441d42bc-f5b7-4be7-b76d-98c92279b384?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more rainfall, as well. For every degree of warming, the atmosphere can [hold](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6f1292-3fa4-4aa4-96b6-85a1f94c8b10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 7 percent more water vapor that could fall as rain. For example, a [study](https://substack.com/redirect/c891ba41-eda0-43a5-a081-66219367ca32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) funded by the Energy Department looking at Hurricane Ida concluded that climate change was directly responsible for up to half a million people's exposure to the storm's floodwaters.
Coastal storms are also becoming more dangerous due to rising seas, whose levels have [increased](https://substack.com/redirect/aeb25c10-fdef-45fd-984d-6435b2df6bdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eight to nine inches since 1880, and may rise [multiple feet](https://substack.com/redirect/be75e4ab-f4b9-42db-ac71-631b30080296?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during this century. A [study](https://substack.com/redirect/6c552ecf-e601-495c-982a-21f7e35587b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Hurricane Sandy estimated that sea level rise increased the likelihood of flooding in that storm by 300 percent.
Big Oil companies were fully aware that climate change would make coastal storms like these more dangerous. In 1989, Shell Oil Company produced a [confidential planning document](https://substack.com/redirect/d9175b91-e8a1-4e53-a30c-43ee857376b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that predicted, based on "conventional and probably conservative" assumptions, that the continued burning of fossil fuels would cause "more violent weather," including "more storms" and "more deluges."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/65c27d84-7998-488f-96a7-baca3c3a03c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From Shell confidential group planning document, page 36.
In fact, Big Oil companies demonstrated their understanding of and belief in these scientific conclusions by [modifying](https://substack.com/redirect/6120f4bd-5a1b-4f67-8f46-32d042c8a95c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their own infrastructure, often at significant expense, to prepare for the coming reality of worsening storms and rising sea levels. In the 1990s, engineers working for Shell, Exxon, and ConocoPhillips [noted](https://substack.com/redirect/6120f4bd-5a1b-4f67-8f46-32d042c8a95c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in design specifications for natural gas pipelines that there could be a "considerable increase of the frequency of storms as a result of climate change," even specifying for one offshore natural gas platform that an "estimated rise in water level, due to global warming, of 0.5 meters may be assumed" for the project's 25-year lifespan.
Even as these firms were taking action to protect their own assets from the climate harms they knew were coming, these same companies were engaging in massive disinformation campaigns to, as one fossil fuel coalition's [internal strategy document](https://substack.com/redirect/2cb6803e-ee8b-4b8f-867f-17bed322d42c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) put it, "reposition global warming as theory (not fact)." In the [words](https://substack.com/redirect/4ac81ce2-169b-44fd-ae76-10d4b414889a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of former Senator Chuck Hagel, who championed anti-climate legislation when he was in Congress: "They lied.... It would have put the United States and the world on a whole different track, and today we would have been so much further ahead than we are. It's cost this country, and it cost the world."
One of these costs is the carefree summers of our past. Big Oil stole them from us. So over the next few months, if--or more likely when--you find yourself baking under the sun of a record-breaking heat wave that's making it impossible to enjoy your favorite summer activities, or stuck inside because the air outdoors is dangerously smoky from wildfires near and far, keep in mind that this didn't just happen. Our summers haven't simply gotten worse. They have been made worse by specific companies that knew that what they were doing would ruin summer and went ahead and did it anyway. We shouldn't let them get away with it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f8d76b12-12ae-4d9a-a5e4-8bd6b3698ce5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This piece was published by _[The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/370fad48-bff4-4ee8-8023-cdafe2daba97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. They rock, check 'em out!

To put it bluntly, Big Oil is ruining summer. Naturally, the most obvious threat is the heat. The last three summers have been the ever recorded. Since 1985, have experienced an increase in the number of days with a heat index of 90 degrees or higher. Scientists are increasingly able to determine the degree to which the emissions of particular oil and gas companies have contributed to particular heat waves. For example, a published last fall in the prestigious journal Nature analyzed a number of major heat waves, including the extreme heat that hit the American Southwest in July 2023. And it's not just that these companies contributed to the oppressive heat that is now defining summer for so many of us--it's that they knew full well what they were doing. Pete Hegseth is playing favorites and passing over qualified Black and female servicemembers for promotions, and targeting them for demotion and dismissal—while also promoting inexperienced MAGA loyalists. Nearly 60 percent of the senior officers fired by Hegseth are female or Black. Women and racial minorities in our military have been denied promotions, baselessly fired or dismissed, or have been pushed out of the ranks at alarming and unprecedented rates. Rewarding loyalty to MAGA above the experience, expertise, and exemplary service of the men and women who have dedicated their lives to our country is both despicable and dangerous. [] This isn’t about DEI, racial equity, or even just basic human decency: Pete Hegseth’s unsteady, bigoted, and dangerous leadership of the Department of Defense is putting every single one of us at risk. Hegseth has unraveled the merit-based system that kept our military strong for generations. He’s turning our military into a MAGA loyalty clown show. I pledge to you: When I am elected to the United States Senate, I will make it my personal mission to shut this foolishness down and get back to putting experienced personnel in the positions that matter most . I am Jamie Davis, a third-generation family farmer running to defeat MAGA extremism in this wide open US Senate seat in Louisiana. Together we can make history, flip this seat, and reclaim the US Senate for Democrats. Will you make a donation of $15, $25 or any amount to help me and my team pull off an upset victory this midterm election? name: AOC
subject: Someone who’s fighting for us.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
That's what I want.
#
People always try to make this debate: _“Is so-and-so the future of the Democratic Party?”_ What does that even mean?
I’d rather spend my time talking about how we can actually win. That’s the conversation I’m interested in having.
**How about we ask what _issues_ are the future of the Democratic Party?**
How about we ask is guaranteed healthcare the future of the Democratic Party? Is banning insider trading by members of Congress the future of the Democratic Party? Is putting limits on lobbying the future of the Democratic Party?
They never ask about the issues — and that’s on purpose, because then it’s about what we’re saying. It’s about the agenda that speaks to people.
Wouldn’t you rather elect someone who’s trying to do those things — someone who’s working for _us_ and not for special interests?
**That’s what I want. Someone who’s trying. Someone who’s fighting for us.**
The _people_ define the Democratic Party. Not the DNC. Not incumbents.
And in the last few weeks, the _people_ chose Chris Rabb, Sam Forstag, and Dr. Adam Ramawy — brawlers for the working-class who won by being clear about what they were fighting _for_ — to represent them.
**We can keep this momentum going**. But it's up to each and every one of us to do it.

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132949208/626219667/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDYxOWY3MS03MDYzLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=D4vRE8GknF0TKvYcTqTdabj1cFYXp7Wumuvi2w8mJ5E=&emci=e1817ea8-5363-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=90619f71-7063-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=14565883)

| | Happy Pride Month! One of my great honors was serving as a Grand Marshal at our local Pride celebration a few years back. Every single time I've marched with fellow El Pasoans in our local parade, I am reminded of a fundamental truth: Pride is, and always has been, about freedom. The freedom to be exactly who you are, to love who you love, and to live openly without fear. **Right now, we are seeing a cruel and coordinated wave of attacks against LGBTQ+ Americans.** Politicians who have no real solutions for the challenges facing everyday families are looking for a scapegoat. Instead of addressing the issues keeping people up at night, they are targeting vulnerable communities and turning our neighbors into political talking points to distract from their own failures. It's part of a broader, dangerous push to control deeply personal decisions about our bodies, our healthcare, and our lives. We have to ask ourselves: **why does a politician, or anyone else, get to decide who we are, how we live, or who we love?** Here in El Paso, we know better. We know our diversity isn't a political talking point — it's our strength. We know that every single person deserves dignity, respect, and the basic right to feel safe in their own hometown. Pride is a celebration, absolutely. But it's also a reminder that there's so much work to do and that everyone deserves the freedom to live and love without fear. We must reject manufactured hate, stand up for one another, and protect every individual's right to live authentically. To our LGBTQ+ neighbors, friends, and family: _you belong here, you are loved, and I will always fight alongside you._ With gratitude, _Veronica_ | Donate Today If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Veronica Escobar instantly:

| | **Alexandra Duarte Declares Victory in Senate District 4**
---
| **Modesto, CA — June 8, 2026 —** With more than a 9,000 vote lead after the latest vote counts in Senate District 4, Alexandra Duarte has declared victory in her primary challenge to Senator Marie Alvarado-Gil and will advance to the general election to face progressive activist Jaron Brandon, a Tuolumne County Supervisor. Republican candidates received nearly 60% of the vote in this primary, more than they did in 2024 when President Trump carried the district by roughly 12 points over Kamala Harris. Such a margin, makes Duarte a decisive favorite to win the November election.

“I am honored to earn the support of working families from El Dorado Hills to Death Valley, Patterson to Madera Ranchos and everywhere in between” said Duarte “I view the decisive margin in this election as a clear mandate for Sacramento: it’s time to change. Voters are done paying more for groceries, gas, and insurance, and getting less. Now it’s time to win in November, so that we can deliver.” “I also want to congratulate Senator Marie-Alvarado on a spirited campaign and thank her for her public service.”

“To win a Primary over a incumbent Senator is really rare,” said Duarte campaign consultant Duane Dichiara, “It really speaks to Alexandra’s strength as a candidate and her laser focus on the cost of living. Voters have had enough of high prices and they trust Alexandra to bring them down by pushing back on Sacramento’s extreme one-party agenda.”

“This district has a 5 point Republican registration advantage for Republicans; for Republican candidates to win the partisan vote share by almost 20 points in this primary shows how many independent and Democrat voters agree and how much Alexandra’s focus on the cost of living resonated compared to Jaron Brandon’s focus on far left social issues.”

Duarte raised more than 1 million dollars in the primary and enters the general election with momentum, funding, and bipartisan support. ###

name: Sidni Worth
subject: A job unlike any other...
body:
Dear Peter,

Serving as a Redwoods Rising apprentice is a job unlike any other.

I’ve worked hands-on in forest management and restoration. I’ve stood beneath towering redwoods once damaged by decades of logging and been part of taking important steps to bring those same forests back towards an old growth state. I’ve gained incredible professional and personal experience that I continue to carry with me.

The Apprenticeship Program was originally made possible through private support from people who believed in investing in the next generation of environmental leaders. Today, much of the funding comes from public sources—but with funding for conservation dwindling, it puts these apprenticeships at risk of disappearing.

Private funding from donors like you is essential to keep these opportunities alive for students like me who are passionate about restoration, science, and caring for the redwoods. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM6&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

TRAIN THE NEXT GENERATION [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM6&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

I can tell you first-hand that this experience left its mark on me. I was part of laying the groundwork for restoration work that will help these forests heal and thrive in the years to come. At the same time, I laid the groundwork for my own passions and a career that continues to grow.

Your support will ensure future apprentices can have the chance to learn critical skills, gain field experience, and contribute to the long-term recovery of these forests. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM6&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

My fellow apprentices come from different fields of study and different walks of life, but we all have a passion for the outdoors. We’ve hiked these trails, admired these forests, and fished in these streams. We want to give back and help steward the natural resources that enrich our lives.

Thank you for making this program possible and for investing in the future of the redwoods and the people who will protect them. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM6&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

Sincerely,
Sidni Worth
Redwoods Rising Roads Field Technician I

P.S. The opportunity to get hands-on experience like this is rare. I hope you’ll help keep these apprenticeships available [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM6&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email] to give the next generation of redwood stewards the training they need, so we can care for the forests we all love.

This is cruel and dishonest policy, and we won’t stand for it. That’s why Democrats Win Seats PAC is calling on Congress to reject ANY effort to cut, privatize, weaken, or “reform” Social Security. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132949902/626222361/-933890249?source=DWSPAC_EM_FR_060826_B1_SocialSecurity&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNzFlMzgwNC03NDYzLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=9dRzyXlMX7cMW90c3Yzz8r-fu0P4huwzQh26-nY_HzQ=&emci=ce1e3804-7463-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=d71e3804-7463-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=5260669) It will take a chorus of voices across the country to make a difference, so we need your support! Hey folks,
This one is wild.
A sitting Republican member of Congress has seemingly vanished from public view for months, and somehow almost nobody in Washington seems interested in explaining what's going on. Even Lauren Boebert is calling it out. I dig into the mystery, the silence, and what it says about how broken Congress has become.
* [**00:01:07**] Lauren Boebert publicly questions why a member of Congress hasn't been seen for months--and why nobody seems willing to talk about it.
* [**00:03:48**] I unpack the political incentives behind keeping a vacant seat occupied and why transparency suddenly disappears when power is on the line.

Peter, Pride is celebrated in June because of what happened at the Stonewall Inn on June 28, 1969. Police raided the bar, the latest in a long history of targeting LGBTQ Americans, and this time people stood their ground. The protests lasted for days and one year later the first Pride march was held. At the heart of that moment was the simple idea that what consenting adults do in their private lives is nobody else's business and certainly not the government's. Freedom means protecting everyone's right to live, love, and be themselves without interference. **That idea has never been more American and it has never been more under attack. That's why I'm proud to be endorsed by the Collin County Stonewall Democrats.**

body:
Nearly 50 years later, this friendship still reminds me why we fight together.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132951292/626227603/1328794144?refcode=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5MmIyZTFkLTc4NjMtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=w7uzqZ6pWC-H3auYmVf772rW8xHPOKjwTv9yEsdnwGI=&emci=64c6358f-5a63-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)
---
Today is _National Best Friends Day,_ and I couldn't think of a better way to celebrate than by telling you about the night I met Lily Tomlin. It was 1978. I'd just seen her one-woman show, _Appearing Nitely_ , in Los Angeles, and I was completely blown away. She had me laughing and thinking all evening — and I had to go backstage and meet the woman behind it. I thought I was going to be the starstruck one. But when I walked through the door, Lily was just as surprised to see me. Two artists, full of admiration. And just like that, a friendship was born. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132951293/626227604/2105508926?refcode=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5MmIyZTFkLTc4NjMtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=w7uzqZ6pWC-H3auYmVf772rW8xHPOKjwTv9yEsdnwGI=) It was one of those serendipitous moments you don't realize will change your life. But nearly fifty years later, I can tell you with certainty that meeting Lily changed mine. Since that night, we've shared just about everything — film sets, inside jokes, bad hair days, handcuffs, and more unforgettable moments than I can possibly count. But our friendship has never been just about the laughs. It has always been about showing up when it matters most. Standing side by side at the Women's March in L.A. Protesting the Dakota Access Pipeline. Getting zip-tied together on the steps of the U.S. Capitol. Or just being there when one of us needed a hand to hold. We've always had each other's backs. **And after nearly five decades of friendship, Lily and I have learned the same lesson I’ve learned from this movement:_We are stronger when we show up for each other._** That is what my Climate PAC is all about. People coming together, lifting each other up, meeting our neighbors, and supporting candidates who aren’t even in our states — because we agree that a liveable planet is worth fighting for. JanePAC is bigger than any one of us. It is the more than **50,000 grassroots donors** who keep this work alive. It is the hundreds of climate champions we have helped elect. It is all of us, standing strong together through the power of community. When I look at what we are up against right now — an administration unraveling our democracy, a fossil fuel industry treating our lungs as collateral damage, and a political moment many of us never imagined we would live through — I do not feel hopeless. Because I know who is in this fight with me. So thank you, friend. Thank you for being part of our story. Thank you for showing up. Please take time to connect with the people around you. Get to know your neighbors. Have uncomfortable conversations. Have joyful ones, too. Remind someone they’re not alone with something as simple as a smile. Laughter, friendship, and community are what carry us through moments like this. xx Jane | Before you scroll away, our candidates are up against the oil and gas lobby and the billionaires backing it, all hellbent on protecting a political system that rewards their bottom line. The Jane Fonda Climate PAC exists to disrupt that status quo by unseating politicians in the pocket of corporate polluters and replacing them with climate champions willing to fight like hell for our planet and the communities we call home. **[If a grassroots donation of $5 is within your means, please use this link to join us in the fight for a better future, with better leaders.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132951294/626227605/2105508926?amount=5&refcode=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5MmIyZTFkLTc4NjMtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=w7uzqZ6pWC-H3auYmVf772rW8xHPOKjwTv9yEsdnwGI=)** | [**DONATE**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132951295/626227606/2105508926?amount=5&refcode=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.792b2e1d-7863-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5MmIyZTFkLTc4NjMtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=w7uzqZ6pWC-H3auYmVf772rW8xHPOKjwTv9yEsdnwGI=)

clean_body: Nearly 50 years later, this friendship still reminds me why we fight together. | Today is National Best Friends Day, and I couldn't think of a better way to celebrate than by telling you about the night I met Lily Tomlin. It was 1978. I'd just seen her one-woman show, Appearing Nitely , in Los Angeles, and I was completely blown away. She had me laughing and thinking all evening — and I had to go backstage and meet the woman behind it. I thought I was going to be the starstruck one. But when I walked through the door, Lily was just as surprised to see me. Two artists, full of admiration. And just like that, a friendship was born. = It was one of those serendipitous moments you don't realize will change your life. But nearly fifty years later, I can tell you with certainty that meeting Lily changed mine. Since that night, we've shared just about everything — film sets, inside jokes, bad hair days, handcuffs, and more unforgettable moments than I can possibly count. But our friendship has never been just about the laughs. It has always been about showing up when it matters most. Standing side by side at the Women's March in L.A. Protesting the Dakota Access Pipeline. Getting zip-tied together on the steps of the U.S. Capitol. Or just being there when one of us needed a hand to hold. We've always had each other's backs. And after nearly five decades of friendship, Lily and I have learned the same lesson I’ve learned from this movement:We are stronger when we show up for each other. That is what my Climate PAC is all about. People coming together, lifting each other up, meeting our neighbors, and supporting candidates who aren’t even in our states — because we agree that a liveable planet is worth fighting for. JanePAC is bigger than any one of us. It is the more than 50,000 grassroots donors who keep this work alive. It is the hundreds of climate champions we have helped elect. It is all of us, standing strong together through the power of community. When I look at what we are up against right now — an administration unraveling our democracy, a fossil fuel industry treating our lungs as collateral damage, and a political moment many of us never imagined we would live through — I do not feel hopeless. Because I know who is in this fight with me. So thank you, friend. Thank you for being part of our story. Thank you for showing up. Please take time to connect with the people around you. Get to know your neighbors. Have uncomfortable conversations. Have joyful ones, too. Remind someone they’re not alone with something as simple as a smile. Laughter, friendship, and community are what carry us through moments like this. xx Jane | Before you scroll away, our candidates are up against the oil and gas lobby and the billionaires backing it, all hellbent on protecting a political system that rewards their bottom line. The Jane Fonda Climate PAC exists to disrupt that status quo by unseating politicians in the pocket of corporate polluters and replacing them with climate champions willing to fight like hell for our planet and the communities we call home. = | = | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. |
Peter,
Yesterday clips of Trump storming out of an interview with NBC reporter Kristen Welker of Meet the Press went viral.
During the interview, after pushback from Welker on Trump's claims that elections are rigged, he completely lost it--taking off his microphone, spiking it into the ground, stomping on it, calling Welker "crooked or stupid," and then storming off the set.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FMgsckriwcDv-5fuaCZAym3KanaqVisjgN3jPMjN91LN52I1UKLn2iNf1E23W0nlNrt7nrjXxEWKAE5YkCaw9M7KeWlA-914ZllGA0f6GMrnl1rKWZnt9nyBHzrJ-SQs0Gz2KWk0tApuhTkje5eYGl7U-OUfTeBm1ZeDpbOxE4E2HmQZN5_94qq6elWfrUn5Md0o2tbHQzRdWJ6r8mtwDTzoCo7tMG3stqC5_EgULvk=&c=Lsg6YnTtFUpzOor3OB12k9liqjkWnxsVYOzyzWJiMhlXXggkQUh09Q==&ch=SqLmpP3QuDX8LYdKg-E2f5dvymNIhbX01v6JPp7MA6L8vCDbPOuaRA==)
---

This latest episode is just further evidence of Donald Trump's unraveling and it's becoming increasingly violent and dangerous.
He has suspicious bruises on his hands, swollen ankles, and has routinely made visits to Walter Reed hospital for undisclosed reasons. He has bragged about passing multiple "cognitive tests" during the past two years, not realizing he's admitting something far more damning. Doctors don't administer cognitive tests that frequently to check if you're fine. They do it to track how fast you're declining.
He now routinely falls asleep on camera during White House events during the day, while posting hundreds of times on social media throughout the night into early morning hours--posting AI generated pictures of himself as Jesus, threatening to wipe out the enitre Iranian civilization, and so much more.
Early in May, 36 prominent doctors signed a letter warning about Trump's "rapidly worsening, reality-untethered, increasingly dangerous decline." They urged cabinet officials to limit his access to the nuclear codes and called on them to invoke the 25th amendment:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FMgsckriwcDv-5fuaCZAym3KanaqVisjgN3jPMjN91LN52I1UKLn2iNf1E23W0nlNrt7nrjXxEWKAE5YkCaw9M7KeWlA-914ZllGA0f6GMrnl1rKWZnt9nyBHzrJ-SQs0Gz2KWk0tApuhTkje5eYGl7U-OUfTeBm1ZeDpbOxE4E2HmQZN5_94qq6elWfrUn5Md0o2tbHQzRdWJ6r8mtwDZXaE6q4wvHrQnonZu8GR3w=&c=Lsg6YnTtFUpzOor3OB12k9liqjkWnxsVYOzyzWJiMhlXXggkQUh09Q==&ch=SqLmpP3QuDX8LYdKg-E2f5dvymNIhbX01v6JPp7MA6L8vCDbPOuaRA==)

This is why Defend Our Courts is preparing a firewall against Trump's most insidious ambitions. We won't hold our breath and hope for the sycophants surrounding Trump to save us.
Trump is declining, and that makes him more dangerous, not less. An unhinged president with a grudge and nothing left to lose is pulling every lever he can to rig the midterms, cement his legacy, and make his vision for America permanent before the clock runs out.
That's why we're fighting on every front. We're defending and building majorities on state Supreme Courts, the courts with final say over election laws in their states. We're paving the path to reform and rebalance the U.S. Supreme Court by backing Democrats in key House and Senate races this November. And we're doing it all at a scale we've never attempted before.
This fight will be expensive and hard, but it's the only fight that matters. If you believe a declining, desperate Trump is a danger to Democracy, we need you on our side today. After Graham Platner received a "Grahamily" card from supporters, his campaign appeared to lean into a victim narrative amid scandals involving Reddit posts, Kik, his tattoo, women and questions about honesty. The moment shifted into criticism of supporters who remain emotionally attached to Platner despite new allegations, campaign contradictions and questions about his working-class image. Joe Sokol made his way over to Stonington, Maine to speak with a lobsterman about Susan Collins' defense of the industry, Platner's "oysterman" image, veterans, Reddit comments and whether Maine's working class will trust his campaign.

_ Fellow Conservative,

Julie Roginsky joined me today for the kind of crucial, personal conversation we should all have with political allies when we see deeply unsettling behavior. Julie and I, both 50-something, longtime Democratic consultants, talkers, and _Jews_ --though decidedly unreligious and not hugely culturally Jewish--felt it was time to address something that's bothered us both: the increasingly open and virulent anti-Semitism on parts of The Left.
We both think Bibi Netanyahu is a war criminal. A criminal-criminal. And we think AIPAC are a bunch of right-wing Republican clods. But we're seeing conspiracy theories shared by people we know, and by those in our comment sections we don't, who are otherwise progressive. Some blame American Jews for all Israel does. Blame all Israeli Jews for Bibi's crimes (akin to blaming all Americans for Trump's). Some use "Zionist" as a slur similar to "white supremacist," even though their origins and belief systems couldn't be more unalike. (See chart below).
Julie told stories about how she had to flee Russia in the 1980s. How her family was nearly killed while they were in Israel. I talked about the anti-Semitism I encountered growing up in 1970s New York (go see the film "Gentleman's Agreement," if you doubt this). And my family having to escape pogroms from Odessa to Vienna 100+ years ago when they came to this country. We both talked about how this kind of violence always starts with rhetoric and conspiracies, but never ends there.
It was an emotional conversation. But there was no ranting. We wanted people to understand the impact of what's happening on the human beings behind the figures. What figures? The 9,354 anti-Semitic incidents in 2024, the most on record since tracking began in 1979. The fact that Jews, who make up 2% of the U.S., were the targets of 70% of "religion-based hate crimes" in the. U.S. In 2024, according to the FBI. And more.
Gaza is horrific. But so are Sudan, Myanmar, and Syria. China puts Muslims in concentration camps. Saudi Arabia has mass-murdered Yemenis, and has a leader, Mohammed bin Salman who ordered an American green-card holder bonesawed to death. Kills women for the "crime" of being raped. And MBS was every bit as important in convincing Trump to attack Iran as Netanyahu. And the U.S. funds them. Heavily.
But there are no protests standing up for innocent Yemenis against Saudi Arabia on American college campuses, and few articles on Substack. Why? We make a plea for consistency, context and nuance. For understanding not only the moral impact of what we choose to say (and ignore), but the political fallout. Which a certain Russian leader has a keen interest in causing, and he just happens to hail from a country that mastered dividing the West with anti-Semitism in the 1960s. This could crack the Democratic coalition.
Please watch the video, my friends. 🙏 There is much more there.
--Cliff

Julie and I, both 50-something, longtime Democratic consultants, talkers, and Jews --though decidedly unreligious and not hugely culturally Jewish--felt it was time to address something that's bothered us both: the increasingly open and virulent anti-Semitism on parts of The Left. We both think Bibi Netanyahu is a war criminal. A criminal-criminal. And we think AIPAC are a bunch of right-wing Republican clods. But we're seeing conspiracy theories shared by people we know, and by those in our comment sections we don't, who are otherwise progressive. Some blame American Jews for all Israel does. Blame all Israeli Jews for Bibi's crimes (akin to blaming all Americans for Trump's). Some use "Zionist" as a slur similar to "white supremacist," even though their origins and belief systems couldn't be more unalike. (See chart below). Julie told stories about how she had to flee Russia in the 1980s. How her family was nearly killed while they were in Israel. I talked about the anti-Semitism I encountered growing up in 1970s New York (go see the film "Gentleman's Agreement," if you doubt this). And my family having to escape pogroms from Odessa to Vienna 100+ years ago when they came to this country. We both talked about how this kind of violence always starts with rhetoric and conspiracies, but never ends there. It was an emotional conversation. But there was no ranting. We wanted people to understand the impact of what's happening on the human beings behind the figures. What figures? The 9,354 anti-Semitic incidents in 2024, the most on record since tracking began in 1979. The fact that Jews, who make up 2% of the U.S., were the targets of 70% of "religion-based hate crimes" in the. U.S. In 2024, according to the FBI. And more. Gaza is horrific. But so are Sudan, Myanmar, and Syria. China puts Muslims in concentration camps. Saudi Arabia has mass-murdered Yemenis, and has a leader, Mohammed bin Salman who ordered an American green-card holder bonesawed to death. Kills women for the "crime" of being raped. And MBS was every bit as important in convincing Trump to attack Iran as Netanyahu. And the U.S. funds them. Heavily. But there are no protests standing up for innocent Yemenis against Saudi Arabia on American college campuses, and few articles on Substack. Why? We make a plea for consistency, context and nuance. For understanding not only the moral impact of what we choose to say (and ignore), but the political fallout. Which a certain Russian leader has a keen interest in causing, and he just happens to hail from a country that mastered dividing the West with anti-Semitism in the 1960s. This could crack the Democratic coalition. Please watch the video, my friends. 🙏 There is much more there. --Cliff Cliff 's Note: Look--we don't do a conversation like this one for clicks. There's no fun thumbnail here, no easy applause line. Julie and I did it because somebody has to, and because the people funding Blue Amp Media are the only reason we can. That's not a figure of speech. We have no network suits, no billionaire owner, nobody whispering "go easier on this one." It's you. So if this conversation meant something to you, here's how you keep it coming. Become a paid subscriber. It's the single most important thing you can do. Just outside Rome one can still walk the 2000 year-old Via Appia, an ancient road constructed by the Republic for the betterment of the community, a gathering place, and providing a convenient access for migrant communities journeying to city.
That's a lie. Pretty funny one, too, if you consider what the Republic thought about non-Romans. Rome built roads for one purpose and only one purpose: the Legions. Because of the cleared paths and flat surfaces, Rome could move tens of thousands of men, horses, carts and wagons, and supply chains to anywhere in their lands with tremendous speed. This kept the peace and protected Rome for centuries from both domestic and foreign unrest.
That these roads were also used by merchants or traders or farmers or even nobles visiting their villas, is ancillary.
We need to return to the Roman understanding of roads: their purpose in our society is less for the military but the need for efficient, agile, unencumbered movement of people and goods remains paramount. This, too, will keep the peace.
But our roads are under attacks, and this time, by the leaders of our Republic. Our leftist leaders.
One of my favorite regular media appearances is with Fox News' Jimmy Failla who used to be a NYC cab driver, and we often talk about the relentless attack on roads shifting with leftists shifting their purpose from agile movement to community feel-good stupidity, and creating chaos in the process.
Mayor Bloomberg started it with the pedestrian plazas shutting down major intersections, diverting traffic so a southbound car on Broadway is forced to go right, left, left, right to continue straight. He did this to create the hang out spot of Times Square with artist renderings of two women laughing, eating salad in a flower garden. What resulted was streets of masturbating homeless and naked women posing for photos for money.
The cars were so much better.
